sentences.zh: 郎餘令，定州新樂人。

translations.literal: Lang Yuling was a man of Xinle in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Yuling was a native of Xinle in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖穎，字楚之，與兄蔚之俱有名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ying, style name Chuzhi, and his elder brother Weizhi were both famous.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ying, courtesy name Chuzhi, was as renowned as his elder brother Weizhi.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為尚書民曹朗，蔚之位左丞。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he served as Lang of the Min Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue; Weizhi held the post of Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign of Sui, he served as bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, while Weizhi held the left vice directorship.

sentences.zh: 煬帝語稱「二郎」。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang in speech called them "the two Langs."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang addressed them in speech as "the two Langs."

sentences.zh: 武德時，楚之以大理卿封常山郡公，與李綱、陳叔達定律令。

translations.literal: In the Wude era Chuzhi was made Marquis of Changshan Commandery as Grand Judge of Dali, and with Li Gang and Chen Shuda drew up statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era, Chuzhi was ennobled as Duke of Changshan Commandery while serving as chief judge of Dali, and together with Li Gang and Chen Shuda drafted statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 持節諭山東，為竇建德所獲，脅以白刃，終不屈。

translations.literal: Bearing credentials he went to instruct the east of the mountains, was captured by Dou Jiande, threatened with naked blades, yet never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing imperial credentials, he went to instruct the lands east of the mountains, was captured by Dou Jiande, threatened with naked blades, and never yielded.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以老乞身，謚曰平。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he requested retirement on account of age; his posthumous title was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified, he asked to retire on account of age; his posthumous title was Ping.

sentences.zh: 餘令博於學，擢進士第，授霍王元軌府參軍事。

translations.literal: Yuling was broadly learned in scholarship, passed the jinshi examination, and was appointed adjutant in the household of Prince Huo, Li Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling was deeply learned; he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed adjutant in the household of Prince Huo, Li Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 從父知年，亦為王友。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Zhinian also served as a companion of the prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father's younger cousin Zhinian also served as a companion to the prince.

sentences.zh: 元軌每曰：「郎家二賢皆入府，不意培塿而松柏為林也。」

translations.literal: Yuanji would often say: "Two worthies of the Lang family have both entered my household—I never expected that from mere mounds could grow a forest of pines and cedars.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji would often say, "Two worthies of the Lang family have both entered my household—who would have thought that from mere mounds could grow a forest of pines and cedars!

sentences.zh: 徙幽州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be recording secretary of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as recording secretary of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 有為浮屠者，積薪自焚，長史裴煚率官屬將觀焉，餘令曰：「人好生惡死，情也。

translations.literal: There was a Buddhist monk who piled firewood to burn himself; Chief Clerk Pei Jiong led the officials to go witness it. Yuling said: "People love life and hate death—that is human nature.
translations.idiomatic: A Buddhist monk piled firewood to burn himself; Chief Clerk Pei Jiong led the officials to go and watch. Yuling said, "People love life and hate death—that is human nature.

sentences.zh: 彼違蔑教義，反其所欲，公當察之，毋輕往。」

translations.literal: This man violates and scorns religious teaching and acts against what he himself desires; you ought to investigate—do not go lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He violates and scorns religious teaching and acts against what he himself desires; you ought to investigate—do not go lightly.

sentences.zh: 煚試廉按，果得其奸。

translations.literal: Jiong tried an investigation on grounds of integrity and indeed uncovered his fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong investigated on grounds of integrity and indeed uncovered his fraud.

sentences.zh: 孝敬在東宮，餘令以梁元帝有《孝德傳》，更撰《後傳》數十篇獻太子，太子嗟重。

translations.literal: When Xiaojing was in the Eastern Palace, Yuling, because Emperor Yuan of Liang had a Biographies of Filial Virtue, wrote dozens of further chapters as a sequel and presented them to the crown prince, who admired them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaojing was crown prince, Yuling, noting that Emperor Yuan of Liang had written a Biographies of Filial Virtue, composed dozens of sequel chapters and presented them to the heir apparent, who admired them greatly.

sentences.zh: 改著作佐郎，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Drafting Editor and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant drafting editor and then died.

sentences.zh: 兄餘慶，為吏清而刻於法。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yu Qing was a clear-handed official who was severe in the application of law.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yu Qing was an upright official who was severe in the application of law.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，為萬年令，道無掇遺。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong he was magistrate of Wannian; nothing lost on the roads was picked up.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he served as magistrate of Wannian, where nothing lost on the roads was picked up.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中丞，務謙謹下人，引御史坐與議論。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief, was diligent in modesty and deference, and would seat censors beside him for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice censor-in-chief, practiced modesty and deference toward others, and would seat censors beside him for discussion.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎楊思玄倨貴，視選者不以禮，餘慶劾免其官。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yang Sixuan was arrogant and lofty and did not treat candidates with courtesy; Yu Qing impeached and had him removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Sixuan was arrogant and did not treat candidates with courtesy; Yu Qing impeached him and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he went out as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was posted out as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐累下遷交州都督。

translations.literal: Because of accumulated guilt he was demoted to military governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of accumulated offenses he was demoted to military governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 驩州司馬裴敬敷與餘慶雅故，以事笞餘慶婢父，婢方嬖，譖敬敷死獄中。

translations.literal: Huanzhou assistant commandant Pei Jingfu was an old friend of Yu Qing's; on account of some matter he beat the father of Yu Qing's maidservant. The maid was then a favorite and slandered Jingfu until he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Huanzhou assistant commandant Pei Jingfu was an old friend of Yu Qing's; over some matter he beat the father of Yu Qing's maidservant. The maid was then a favorite, and she slandered Jingfu until he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 又裒貨無藝，民詣闕訴之，使者十輩臨按，餘慶謾讕，不能得其情。

translations.literal: He also amassed goods without limit; the people appealed at the capital. Ten rounds of envoys came to investigate, but Yu Qing prevaricated and they could not get at the truth.
translations.idiomatic: He also amassed goods without restraint; the people appealed at the capital. Ten rounds of envoys came to investigate, but Yu Qing prevaricated and they could not get at the truth.

sentences.zh: 最後，廣州都督陳善弘按之，餘慶自恃在朝廷久，明法令，輕善弘，不置對。

translations.literal: Finally Guangzhou military governor Chen Shanhong investigated; Yu Qing, trusting in his long years at court and his mastery of statutes, looked down on Shanhong and would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Guangzhou military governor Chen Shanhong investigated the case; Yu Qing, trusting in his long years at court and his mastery of statutes, looked down on Shanhong and would not respond.

sentences.zh: 善弘怒曰：「舞文弄法，吾不及君；

translations.literal: Shanhong said angrily: "In twisting texts and manipulating the law, I am not your equal;
translations.idiomatic: Shanhong said angrily, "In twisting texts and manipulating the law, I am not your equal;

sentences.zh: 今日以天子命治君，吾力有餘矣。」

translations.literal: but today, with the Son of Heaven's mandate to deal with you, my strength is more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: but today, with the Son of Heaven's mandate to deal with you, my strength is more than enough.

sentences.zh: 欲搒械之，餘慶懼，服罪。

translations.literal: He was about to beat and shackle him; Yu Qing was afraid and confessed.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to beat and shackle him; Yu Qing was afraid and confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 高宗詔放瓊州。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ordered him released to Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong ordered him exiled to Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦當還，朝廷惡其暴，徙春州。

translations.literal: When an amnesty would have allowed his return, the court detested his violence and transferred him to Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty would have allowed his return, the court detested his brutality and transferred him to Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，餘慶治萬年，父知運嫌其酷，將杖之，餘慶避免。

translations.literal: At first, when Yu Qing governed Wannian, his father Zhiyun disliked his harshness and was about to beat him; Yu Qing avoided it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yu Qing governed Wannian, his father Zhiyun disliked his harshness and was about to beat him; Yu Qing avoided the blow.

sentences.zh: 父嘆曰：「國家用之矣，吾尚奈何！」

translations.literal: His father sighed: "The state is already using him—what can I still do!
translations.idiomatic: His father sighed, "The state is already using him—what can I still do!

sentences.zh: 及為御史中丞，復嘆曰：「郎氏危矣！」

translations.literal: When he became Vice Censor-in-Chief, he sighed again: "The Lang clan is in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: When he became vice censor-in-chief, he sighed again, "The Lang clan is in peril!"

sentences.zh: 以憂死。

translations.literal: He died of worry.
translations.idiomatic: He died of worry.

sentences.zh: 餘慶卒以貪殘廢。

translations.literal: Yu Qing ultimately was ruined for greed and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing was ultimately ruined for greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 徐齊聃，字將道，湖州長城人，世客馮翊。

translations.literal: Xu Qichan, style name Jiangdao, was a native of Changcheng in Huzhou; his family had long sojourned in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qichan, courtesy name Jiangdao, was a native of Changcheng in Huzhou; his family had long resided as guests in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 梁慈源侯整四世孫。

translations.literal: He was a fourth-generation descendant of Marquis Zheng of Ciyuan under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fourth-generation descendant of Marquis Zheng of Ciyuan under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 八歲能文，太宗召試，賜所佩金削刀。

translations.literal: At eight he could write; Taizong summoned him for a test and bestowed the gold trimming knife he wore at his belt.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could write; Taizong summoned him for a test and bestowed the gold trimming knife from his own belt.

sentences.zh: 舉弘文生，調曹王府參軍。

translations.literal: He entered as a Hongwen student and was assigned as adjutant in the household of the Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as a Hongwen student and was assigned as adjutant in the household of the Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，為潞王府文學、崇文館學士，侍皇太子講，修書於芳林門。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong he was literary tutor to the Prince of Lu and scholar of the Chongwen Hall, attending the crown prince's lectures and compiling books at the Fanglin Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he served as literary tutor to the Prince of Lu and as a Chongwen Hall scholar, attending the crown prince's lectures and compiling books at the Fanglin Gate.

sentences.zh: 時姑為帝婕妤，嫌以恩進，故求出為桃林令。

translations.literal: At the time his aunt was the emperor's jieyu; he shrank from advancement through favor and therefore sought a post outside as magistrate of Taolin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his aunt was the emperor's jieyu; he shrank from advancement through favor and therefore sought an outside post as magistrate of Taolin.

sentences.zh: 召為沛王侍讀，再遷司議郎，皆不就。

translations.literal: He was summoned as reader-attendant to the Prince of Pei and twice promoted to Gentleman for Discussion of Policy, but refused both.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as reader-attendant to the Prince of Pei and twice promoted to Gentleman for Discussion of Policy, but declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 累進西臺舍人。

translations.literal: He rose to drafter of the Western Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to drafter of the Western Terrace.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，詔突厥酋長子弟得事東宮，齊聃上書諫，以為：「氈裘冒頓之裔，解辮削衽，使在左右，非所謂『恭慎威儀，以近有德』、『任官惟賢才，左右惟其人』之義。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng an edict allowed sons and younger brothers of Türk chieftains to serve in the Eastern Palace. Qichan submitted a memorial of remonstrance, holding that: "Descendants of Modun in felt robes, with queues cut and robes altered, placed at one's left and right, is not what is meant by 'Reverent and cautious in bearing, to draw near the virtuous' or 'In appointing offices, only the talented; at one's side, only the right men.'
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianheng, an edict allowed sons and younger brothers of Türk chieftains to serve in the Eastern Palace. Qichan submitted a memorial of remonstrance, arguing that placing descendants of Modun in felt robes, with queues cut and robes altered, at one's left and right was not what was meant by "Reverent and cautious in bearing, to draw near the virtuous" or "In appointing offices, only the talented; at one's side, only the right men.

sentences.zh: 又長孫無忌以讒死，家廟毀頓，齊聃言於帝曰：「齊獻公，陛下外祖，雖後嗣有罪，不宜毀及先廟。

translations.literal: Further, when Zhangsun Wuji died through slander and his family temple fell into ruin, Qichan said to the emperor: "Duke Xian of Qi was Your Majesty's maternal grandfather; though later descendants were guilty, the ancestral temple ought not to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangsun Wuji died through slander and his family temple fell into ruin, Qichan said to the emperor, "Duke Xian of Qi was Your Majesty's maternal grandfather; though later descendants were guilty, the ancestral temple ought not to be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今周忠孝公廟反崇飾逾制，恐非所以示海內。」

translations.literal: Now the temple of Duke Zhongxiao of Zhou is instead over-adorned beyond regulation—I fear this is not how to show the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the temple of Duke Zhongxiao of Zhou is instead over-adorned beyond regulation—I fear this is not how to show the realm what is right."

sentences.zh: 帝寤，有詔復獻公官，以無忌孫延主其祀。

translations.literal: The emperor awoke to this; an edict restored the Duke of Qi's offices and made Wuji's grandson Yan head his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took heed; an edict restored the Duke of Qi's offices and made Wuji's grandson Yan head his sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 齊聃善文誥，帝愛之，令侍皇太子及諸王屬文，以職樞劇，許間日一至。

translations.literal: Qichan excelled at literary edicts; the emperor favored him and ordered him to attend the crown prince and princes in literary matters. Because the post was critically busy, he was permitted to come every other day.
translations.idiomatic: Qichan excelled at literary edicts; the emperor favored him and ordered him to attend the crown prince and the princes in literary matters. Because the post was critically demanding, he was permitted to come every other day.

sentences.zh: 坐漏禁中事，貶蘄州司馬。

translations.literal: He was demoted to assistant commandant of Qizhou for leaking inner-palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to assistant commandant of Qizhou for leaking inner-palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 又流欽州。

translations.literal: He was further exiled to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further exiled to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十四。

translations.literal: He died at forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Under Ruizong he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ruizong he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子堅。

translations.literal: His son was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅，字元固，幼有敏性。

translations.literal: Jian, style name Yuangu, had quick wit as a child.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, courtesy name Yuangu, had quick wit as a child.

sentences.zh: 沛王聞其名，召見，授紙為賦，異之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pei heard his fame, summoned and met him, gave him paper to compose a fu, and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pei heard of his reputation, summoned him, gave him paper to compose a fu, and marveled at the result.

sentences.zh: 十四而孤，及壯，寬厚長者。

translations.literal: Orphaned at fourteen, when grown he was a generous and long-suffering elder.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at fourteen, when grown he was a generous and forbearing man of stature.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才及第，為汾州參軍事，遷萬年主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the xiucai examination, served as adjutant of Fenzhou, and was promoted to recorder of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the xiucai examination, served as adjutant of Fenzhou, and was promoted to recorder of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 天授三年，上言：「書有五聽，令有三覆，慮失情也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshou he memorialized: "The Book of Documents speaks of five modes of hearing; ordinances speak of three reviews—this is from concern lest emotion be missed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianshou he memorialized, "The Book of Documents speaks of five modes of hearing; ordinances speak of three reviews—this is from concern lest the true circumstances be missed.

sentences.zh: 比犯大逆，詔使者勘當，得實輒決。

translations.literal: Lately, in cases of great treason, edicts send emissaries to investigate; once the facts are found, judgment is immediate.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, in cases of great treason, edicts send emissaries to investigate; once the facts are found, judgment is immediate.

sentences.zh: 人命至重，萬有一不實，欲訴無由，以就赤族，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Human life is supremely weighty; if in ten thousand cases there is one that is not true, there is no means to appeal and the whole clan goes to execution—is this not agonizing!
translations.idiomatic: Human life is supremely weighty; if in ten thousand cases there is one that is not true, there is no means to appeal and the whole clan goes to execution—is this not agonizing!

sentences.zh: 此不足檢下之奸亂，適長使人威福耳。

translations.literal: This is insufficient to restrain wickedness below—it only nourishes the power and favor of agents.
translations.idiomatic: This is insufficient to restrain wickedness below—it only nourishes the power and favor of agents.

sentences.zh: 臣請如令覆奏，則死者無恨。

translations.literal: Your subject asks that, as the ordinance provides, cases be reviewed in memorial to the throne; then the dead would have no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that, as the ordinance provides, cases be reviewed in memorial to the throne; then the condemned would have no cause for resentment.

sentences.zh: 又古者罰不逮嗣，故卻芮亂國而缺升諸朝，嵇康蒙戮而紹死於難，則於它親不復致疑。

translations.literal: Again, in antiquity punishment did not reach descendants; thus though Que and Rui threw the state into disorder, Que was still raised in court, and though Ji Kang suffered execution, Shao died in the disaster—so toward other kin no further suspicion was raised.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in antiquity punishment did not reach descendants; thus though Que and Rui threw the state into disorder, Que was still raised in court, and though Ji Kang suffered execution, Shao died in the disaster—so toward other kin no further suspicion was raised.

sentences.zh: 今選部廣責逆人親屬，至無服者尚數十條。

translations.literal: Now the Selection Bureau broadly blames the kin of traitors—even for kin beyond mourning dress there are still dozens of clauses.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Selection Bureau broadly blames the kin of traitors—even for kin beyond mourning dress there are still dozens of clauses.

sentences.zh: 且詔書『與逆同堂親不任京畿，緦麻親不得侍衛』，臣請如詔書外，一切不禁，以申曠蕩。」

translations.literal: Moreover the edict reads, 'Kin in the same hall as traitors may not hold office in the capital region; kin in fine hemp mourning may not serve as guards.' Your subject asks that beyond what the edict states, everything not be forbidden, to express magnanimous ease."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the edict reads, 'Kin in the same hall as traitors may not hold office in the capital region; kin in fine hemp mourning may not serve as guards.' Your subject asks that beyond what the edict states, everything else not be forbidden, to express magnanimous ease."

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，東都留守楊再思、王方慶共引為判官。

translations.literal: In the Shengli era, Eastern Capital regents Yang Zaisi and Wang Fangqing together brought him in as judicial aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengli era, Eastern Capital regents Yang Zaisi and Wang Fangqing together brought him in as judicial aide.

sentences.zh: 方慶善《禮》學，嘗就質疑晦，堅為申釋，常得所未聞。

translations.literal: Fangqing was versed in the Rites; he would come to Jian with obscure doubts, and Jian would explain them—often giving what Fangqing had never heard.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing was versed in the Rites; he would come to Jian with obscure doubts, and Jian would explain them—often giving Fangqing what he had never heard.

sentences.zh: 屬文典厚，再思每目為鳳閣舍人樣。

translations.literal: His compositions were classical and substantial; Zaisi would call him the model of a Phoenix Pavilion drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His compositions were classical and substantial; Zaisi would call him the model of a Phoenix Pavilion drafter.

sentences.zh: 與徐彥伯、劉知幾、張說與修《三教珠英》，時張昌宗、李嶠總領，彌年不下筆，堅與說專意撰綜，條匯粗立，諸儒因之，乃成書。

translations.literal: With Xu Yanbo, Liu Zhiji, and Zhang Yue he compiled the Pearl Grove of the Three Teachings; at the time Zhang Changzong and Li Jiao oversaw it, and for a full year no one set brush to paper. Jian and Yue concentrated on drafting and synthesis; outlines were roughly set, the various scholars followed up, and the book was completed.
translations.idiomatic: With Xu Yanbo, Liu Zhiji, and Zhang Yue he compiled the Pearl Grove of the Three Teachings; Zhang Changzong and Li Jiao oversaw the project, and for a full year no one set brush to paper. Jian and Yue concentrated on drafting and synthesis; outlines were roughly set, the other scholars followed up, and the book was completed.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中，封慈源縣子。

translations.literal: He rose to Supervising Censor and was ennobled as Viscount of Ciyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervising censor and was ennobled as Viscount of Ciyuan.

sentences.zh: 中宗怒韋月將，欲即斬之，堅奏盛夏生長，請須秋乃決，時申救者亦眾，得以搒死。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was angry at Wei Yuejiang and wished to behead him immediately; Jian memorialized that in midsummer things grow—he asked that execution wait until autumn. Many at the time also pleaded for mercy; he was spared instant death but beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was angry at Wei Yuejiang and wished to behead him at once; Jian memorialized that in midsummer all things grow and asked that execution wait until autumn. Many at the time also pleaded for mercy; Wei was spared instant death but was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 俄以禮部侍郎為修文館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Scholar of the Hall for Cultivation of Letters as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made a scholar of the Hall for Cultivation of Letters while serving as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，授太子左庶子兼崇文館學士，修史，進東海郡公，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Jian was made Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently scholar of the Chongwen Hall, compiled history, was advanced to Duke of the Eastern Sea, and moved to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Jian was made left mentor of the heir apparent and concurrently a Chongwen Hall scholar, compiled history, was advanced to Duke of the Eastern Sea, and was promoted to vice minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史李知古兵擊姚州渳河蠻，降之，又請築城，使輸賦徭。

translations.literal: At the time investigating censor Li Zhigu led troops against the Mi River barbarians of Yaozhou, subdued them, and also asked to build walls and make them submit taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At the time investigating censor Li Zhigu led troops against the Mi River barbarians of Yaozhou, subdued them, and also asked to build fortifications and make them submit taxes and corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 堅議：「蠻夷羈縻以屬，不宜與中國同法，恐勞師遠伐，益不償損。」

translations.literal: Jian argued: "Barbarians are attached by loose reins—they should not be subject to the same laws as China; I fear laboring the army on distant campaigns where the losses will exceed the gain.
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued, "Barbarians are held by loose reins of attachment—they should not be subject to the same laws as China; I fear laboring the army on distant campaigns where the losses will exceed the gain.

sentences.zh: 不聽，詔知古發劍南兵築城堡，列州縣。

translations.literal: His advice was not followed; an edict ordered Zhigu to raise troops from Jiannan, build forts, and set up prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded; an edict ordered Zhigu to raise troops from Jiannan, build fortifications, and establish prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 知古因是欲誅其豪酋，入子女為奴婢，蠻懼，殺知古，相率潰叛，姚、巂路閉不通者數年。

translations.literal: Zhigu took this occasion to wish to execute their great chiefs and bring sons and daughters in as slaves; the barbarians feared this, killed Zhigu, and fled in revolt one after another; the roads through Yao and Xi were closed for years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu took this occasion to seek to execute their great chiefs and bring sons and daughters in as slaves; the barbarians feared this, killed Zhigu, and fled in revolt one after another; the roads through Yao and Xi were closed for years.

sentences.zh: 初，太平公主用事，武攸暨屢邀請堅，堅不許。

translations.literal: At first, when Princess Taiping held power, Wu Youqi repeatedly invited Jian, but Jian would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Princess Taiping held power, Wu Youqi repeatedly invited Jian, but Jian would not agree.

sentences.zh: 又以妻岑羲女弟，固辭機密，轉太子詹事，曰：「吾非求高，逃禍耳。」

translations.literal: Also, because his wife was the younger sister of Cen Xi's daughter, he firmly declined confidential posts and was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, saying: "I am not seeking elevation—I am fleeing disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Also, because his wife was the younger sister of Cen Xi's daughter, he firmly declined confidential posts and was transferred to grand mentor of the heir apparent, saying, "I am not seeking elevation—I am fleeing disaster.

sentences.zh: 羲敗，不染於惡，出為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xi fell, Jian was not stained by the evil and went out as prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi fell, Jian was not stained by the evil and was posted out as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 數外徙，久乃遷秘書監、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After several external transfers, long afterward he was made Director of the Palace Library and Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After several external transfers, long afterward he was made director of the Palace Library and left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 玄宗改麗正書院為集賢院，以堅充學士，副張說知院事。

translations.literal: Xuanzong changed the Lizheng Academy to the Jixian Academy and made Jian a scholar, assisting Zhang Yue in directing the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong changed the Lizheng Academy to the Jixian Academy and made Jian a scholar, assisting Zhang Yue in directing the academy.

sentences.zh: 帝大酺集賢，幔舍在百司上，說令揭大榜以侈其寵，堅見，遽命撤之，曰：「君子烏取多尚人！」

translations.literal: The emperor held a grand feast for the Jixian scholars; their curtained lodges stood above all offices. Yue had a great placard posted to display his favor; when Jian saw it, he immediately ordered it removed, saying: "What gentleman courts excess to impress others!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held a grand feast for the Jixian scholars; their curtained lodges stood above all the other offices. Yue had a great placard posted to display his favor; when Jian saw it, he immediately ordered it removed, saying, "What gentleman courts excess to impress others!

sentences.zh: 從上泰山，以參定儀典，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor to Mount Tai, assisted in fixing ritual codes, and was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Mount Tai, assisted in fixing the ritual codes, and was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 堅於典故多所諳識，凡七當撰次高選。

translations.literal: Jian was well versed in many precedents and ordinances; seven times he was chosen for high compilation work.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was well versed in many precedents and ordinances; seven times he was chosen for major compilation work.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十餘，帝悼惜，遣使就吊，贈太子少保，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He died in his seventies; the emperor mourned him, sent envoys to offer condolences at his home, posthumously made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies; the emperor mourned him, sent envoys to offer condolences at his home, posthumously made him junior mentor of the heir apparent, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 齊聃姑為太宗充容，仲為高宗婕妤，皆明圖史，議者以堅父子如漢班氏。

translations.literal: Qichan's elder aunt was a palace lady filling the role of rong for Taizong; his younger aunt was a jieyu for Gaozong—both were versed in maps and histories; opinion likened Jian and his father to the Ban family of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Qichan's elder aunt served Taizong as a palace lady of rong; his younger aunt served Gaozong as a jieyu—both were versed in maps and histories; opinion likened Jian and his father to the Ban family of Han.

sentences.zh: 子嶠，字巨山。

translations.literal: His son was Qiao, style name Jushan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qiao, courtesy name Jushan.

sentences.zh: 開元中為駕部員外郎、集賢院直學士，遷中書舍人、內供奉、河南尹。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was Vice Director in the Ministry of Transport and a direct scholar of the Jixian Academy, then promoted to Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat, inner attendant, and governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he served as vice director in the Ministry of Transport and as a direct scholar of the Jixian Academy, then was promoted to drafting secretary of the Central Secretariat, inner attendant, and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 封慈源縣公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Ciyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title of Duke of Ciyuan County.

sentences.zh: 父子相次為學士，自祖及孫，三世為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Father and son successively served as academicians; from grandfather to grandson, three generations served as Secretariat Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son served as academicians in succession, and for three generations—from grandfather to grandson—the family held the post of Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 沈伯儀，湖州吳興人。

translations.literal: Shen Boyi was a native of Wuxing in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Boyi came from Wuxing in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 武後時，為太子右諭德。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, he served as Right Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, he served as Right Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 初，太常少卿韋萬石議明堂大享事，上言：「鄭玄說祀五天帝，王肅謂祀五行帝。

translations.literal: Initially, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Wei Wanshi discussed the grand offerings at the Bright Hall and submitted a memorial stating: "Zheng Xuan held that one should sacrifice to the Five Heavenly Emperors; Wang Su maintained that one should sacrifice to the Five Elemental Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Wei Wanshi raised the question of the grand Bright Hall offerings in a memorial: Zheng Xuan taught that one sacrificed to the Five Heavenly Emperors, while Wang Su argued for sacrifice to the Five Elemental Emperors.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀禮》從玄，至《顯慶禮》祀昊天上帝，乾封詔書祀五天帝兼祀昊天，上元詔書從《貞觀禮》，儀鳳初詔祀事一用周制。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Rites followed Xuan; by the Xianqing Rites sacrifice was made to August Heaven, the Supreme Lord; the Qianfeng edict ordered sacrifice to the Five Heavenly Emperors together with August Heaven; the Shangyuan edict followed the Zhenguan Rites; at the beginning of the Yifeng reign an edict ordered that all sacrificial rites follow the Zhou system.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites had followed Zheng Xuan; the Xianqing Rites turned to worship of August Heaven, the Supreme Lord; a Qianfeng edict mandated both the Five Heavenly Emperors and August Heaven; a Shangyuan edict reverted to the Zhenguan model; and at the start of Yifeng all sacrifices were ordered to follow Zhou practice.

sentences.zh: 今應何樂？」

translations.literal: Which rites should be followed now?"
translations.idiomatic: Which standard should govern the rites now?

sentences.zh: 高宗乃詔尚書省集諸儒議，未能定。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong then ordered the Department of State Affairs to gather the Ru scholars for discussion, but no decision could be reached.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong then ordered the Department of State Affairs to assemble the Confucian scholars for debate, but they could not settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 於是大享參用《貞觀》、《顯慶》二禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the grand offerings combined both the Zhenguan and Xianqing rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, the grand offerings drew on both the Zhenguan and Xianqing rites.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年，成均助教孔玄義奏：「嚴父莫大配天，天於萬物為最大，推父偶天，孝之大，尊之極也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong, Kong Xuanyi, Assistant Instructor at the Imperial Academy, submitted a memorial: "There is no greater expression of honoring one's father than pairing him with Heaven; among all things Heaven is greatest; elevating the father to stand paired with Heaven is the highest filial piety and the utmost honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chuigong, Kong Xuanyi, assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy, submitted a memorial: "No honor surpasses pairing one's father with Heaven. Heaven is supreme among all things, and to exalt the father beside Heaven is the greatest filial devotion and the highest mark of reverence.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱『先王作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖、考』。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, 'The former kings made music to exalt virtue; the Yin people presented offerings to the Supreme Lord, pairing their ancestors and forefathers.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The former kings made music to glorify virtue; the Yin people offered to the Supreme Lord, pairing their ancestors and forefathers."

sentences.zh: 上帝，天也。

translations.literal: The Supreme Lord is Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Lord is Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 昊天之祭，宜祖、考並配，請以太宗、高宗配上帝於圓丘，神堯皇帝配感帝南郊。

translations.literal: In the sacrifice to August Heaven, ancestors and forefathers should both be paired; I request that Emperor Taizong and Emperor Gaozong be paired with the Supreme Lord at the circular altar, and Emperor Shenyao be paired with the Lord of Sensation at the southern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: In sacrifices to August Heaven, both ancestors and forefathers ought to be paired; I propose that Emperor Taizong and Emperor Gaozong be paired with the Supreme Lord at the Circular Altar, and Emperor Shenyao with the Lord of Sensation at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 《祭法》：『祖文王，宗武王。』

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifices states: 'Take King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrifices says: "Take King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong."

sentences.zh: 祖，始也；

translations.literal: Zu means 'the beginning';
translations.idiomatic: Zu means "the beginning";

sentences.zh: 宗，尊也。

translations.literal: zong means 'the honored.'
translations.idiomatic: zong means "the honored."

sentences.zh: 一名而有二義。

translations.literal: One term has two meanings.
translations.idiomatic: The same term carries two distinct meanings.

sentences.zh: 《經》稱『宗祀文王』，文王當祖而雲宗，包武王以言也。

translations.literal: The Classic says 'sacrificial honoring of King Wen as zong'; King Wen should be taken as zu yet is called zong, which includes King Wu in the reference.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic speaks of "honoring King Wen as zong," yet King Wen should be zu—calling him zong embraces King Wu in the same phrase.

sentences.zh: 知明堂以祖、考配，與二經合。」

translations.literal: Thus one knows that pairing ancestors and forefathers in the Bright Hall accords with both Classics."
translations.idiomatic: This shows that pairing ancestors and forefathers in the Bright Hall agrees with both texts.

sentences.zh: 伯儀曰：「有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，祖顓頊而宗堯；

translations.literal: Boyi said: "The House of Yu performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Ku at the suburb, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yao as zong;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Boyi replied: "The Yu dynasty performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Ku at the suburban altar, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yao as zong;

sentences.zh: 夏後氏禘黃帝而郊鯀，祖顓頊而宗禹；

translations.literal: The House of Xia performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Gun at the suburb, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yu as zong;
translations.idiomatic: The Xia performed di to the Yellow Emperor and jiao to Gun at the suburban altar, took Zhuanxu as zu and Yu as zong;

sentences.zh: 殷人禘嚳而郊冥，祖契而宗湯；

translations.literal: the Yin people performed di to Ku and jiao to Ming at the suburb, took Qi as zu and Tang as zong;
translations.idiomatic: the Yin performed di to Ku and jiao to Ming at the suburban altar, took Qi as zu and Tang as zong;

sentences.zh: 周人禘嚳而郊稷，祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: the Zhou people performed di to Ku and jiao to Hou Ji at the suburb, took King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong.
translations.idiomatic: the Zhou performed di to Ku and jiao to Hou Ji at the suburban altar, took King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：『禘、郊、祖、宗，皆配食也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: 'Di, jiao, zu, and zong are all paired offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: "Di, jiao, zu, and zong are all paired offerings.

sentences.zh: 祭昊天圓丘曰禘，祭上帝南郊曰郊，祭五帝、五神明堂曰祖、宗。』

translations.literal: Sacrifice at the circular altar to August Heaven is called di; sacrifice to the Supreme Lord at the southern suburb is called jiao; sacrifice to the Five Emperors and Five Spirits in the Bright Hall is called zu and zong.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice at the Circular Altar to August Heaven is di; sacrifice to the Supreme Lord at the southern suburb is jiao; sacrifice to the Five Emperors and Five Spirits in the Bright Hall is zu and zong.

sentences.zh: 此為最詳。

translations.literal: This is the most detailed account.
translations.idiomatic: This is the most detailed account.

sentences.zh: 虞夏退顓頊郊嚳，殷舍契郊冥，去取違舛，惟周得禮之序，至明堂始兩配焉。

translations.literal: Yu and Xia set aside Zhuanxu for jiao to Ku; Yin omitted Qi for jiao to Ming—their choices diverged and erred; only Zhou obtained the proper ritual sequence, and only at the Bright Hall did dual pairing begin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Xia displaced Zhuanxu to sacrifice jiao to Ku; Yin set aside Qi for jiao to Ming—their choices were inconsistent and wrong. Only Zhou preserved the proper ritual order, and only at the Bright Hall did dual pairing begin.

sentences.zh: 文王上配五帝，武王下配五神，別父子也。

translations.literal: King Wen was paired above with the Five Emperors; King Wu was paired below with the Five Spirits—thus father and son were distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen was paired above with the Five Emperors and King Wu below with the Five Spirits, distinguishing father from son.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：『嚴父莫大於配天。』

translations.literal: The Classic says: 'There is nothing greater than honoring one's father by pairing him with Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: "There is nothing greater than honoring one's father by pairing him with Heaven."

sentences.zh: 又曰：『宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。』

translations.literal: It also says: 'Honor King Wen in sacrifice at the Bright Hall, pairing him with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Honor King Wen in sacrifice at the Bright Hall, pairing him with the Supreme Lord."

sentences.zh: 不言嚴武王以配天，則武王雖在明堂，未齊於配，雖同祭而終為一主也。

translations.literal: It does not speak of honoring King Wu by pairing him with Heaven; thus though King Wu was present in the Bright Hall, he was not equal in pairing, and though both were sacrificed to, in the end there was only one principal.
translations.idiomatic: It does not speak of honoring King Wu by pairing him with Heaven; so although King Wu was included in the Bright Hall rite, he was not equal in rank of pairing. Though both received sacrifice, in the end there was only one principal deity.

sentences.zh: 緯曰：『後稷為天地主，文王為五帝宗。』

translations.literal: The apocryphal text says: 'Hou Ji was lord of Heaven and Earth; King Wen was zong of the Five Emperors.'
translations.idiomatic: An apocryphal text says: "Hou Ji was lord of Heaven and Earth; King Wen was zong of the Five Emperors."

sentences.zh: 若一神而兩祭之，則薦獻數瀆，此神無二主也。

translations.literal: If one spirit received two sacrifices, the repeated offerings would be excessive—there cannot be two principals for one spirit.
translations.idiomatic: If one spirit received two sacrifices, the repeated offerings would be excessive—a single spirit cannot have two principals.

sentences.zh: 貞觀、永徽禮實專配，由顯慶後始兼尊焉。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan and Yonghui rites in fact used exclusive pairing; only after Xianqing did joint honoring begin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan and Yonghui rites in fact used exclusive pairing; only after the Xianqing era did joint honoring begin.

sentences.zh: 今請以高祖配圓丘、方澤，太宗配南北郊，高宗配五天帝。」

translations.literal: I now request that Emperor Gaozu be paired at the Circular Altar and Square Pond, Emperor Taizong at the northern and southern suburbs, and Emperor Gaozong with the Five Heavenly Emperors."
translations.idiomatic: I now propose that Emperor Gaozu be paired at the Circular Altar and Square Pond, Emperor Taizong at the northern and southern suburbs, and Emperor Gaozong with the Five Heavenly Emperors.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人元萬頃、範履冰等議：「今禮昊天上帝等五祀，鹹奉高祖、太宗兼配，以申孝也。

translations.literal: Fengge Attendant Yuan Wanqing, Fan Lubing, and others argued: "In the present rites for August Heaven, the Supreme Lord, and the other five sacrifices, all should have Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Taizong jointly paired, to express filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Fengge Attendants Yuan Wanqing, Fan Lubing, and others argued: "In the present rites for August Heaven, the Supreme Lord, and the other five sacrifices, Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Taizong should both be paired, to express filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 《詩昊天》章『二後受之』，《易》『薦上帝，配祖、考』，有兼配義。

translations.literal: The Ode to August Heaven chapter says 'the two sovereigns received it'; the Book of Changes says 'present offerings to the Supreme Lord, pairing ancestors and forefathers'—both carry the meaning of joint pairing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ode to August Heaven says "the two sovereigns received it"; the Book of Changes says "present offerings to the Supreme Lord, pairing ancestors and forefathers"—both imply joint pairing.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太宗既先配五祀，當如舊。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Taizong were already first paired in the five sacrifices, the former practice should be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Taizong had already been paired in the five sacrifices, the former practice should stand.

sentences.zh: 請奉高宗歷配焉。」

translations.literal: I request that Emperor Gaozong be paired in succession as well."
translations.idiomatic: I request that Emperor Gaozong be paired in turn as well.

sentences.zh: 自是郊、丘，三帝並配雲。

translations.literal: From then on at the suburban and mound sacrifices, all three emperors were jointly paired.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, at the suburban and mound sacrifices, all three emperors were jointly paired.

sentences.zh: 伯儀歷國子祭酒、修文館學士，卒。

translations.literal: Boyi successively served as Director of the Imperial Academy and Academician of the Xiucheng Hall, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Boyi later served as Director of the Imperial Academy and Academician of the Xiucheng Hall, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 路敬淳，貝州臨清人。

translations.literal: Lu Jingchun was a native of Linqing in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingchun came from Linqing in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 父文逸，遇隋季大亂，闔門死於盜。

translations.literal: His father Wenyi, encountering the great turmoil at the end of the Sui, saw the entire household killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenyi lived through the great turmoil at the end of the Sui, when the whole household was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 文逸遁免，流離辛苦，自傷家多難，閉口不食，行者哀其窮，強飲食之，更負以行，乃得脫。

translations.literal: Wenyi escaped and survived, wandering in hardship; grieving that his family had suffered so many calamities, he closed his mouth and refused to eat; travelers pitied his destitution and forced food upon him, then carried him on their backs as they went, and thus he got away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi alone escaped. Wandering in hardship and grieving the many calamities that had befallen his family, he refused to eat; travelers took pity on his destitution, forced food on him, and carried him on their backs until he finally got away.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，官申州司馬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguan era, he served as Assistant Administrator of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguan era, he served as assistant administrator of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬淳少誌學，足不履門。

translations.literal: Jingchun in his youth was devoted to learning and never stepped outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jingchun was devoted to study and scarcely left his door.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，倚廬不出者三年。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his parents, he lived in a mourning hut and did not go out for three years.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his parents, he lived in a mourning hut and did not go out for three years.

sentences.zh: 服除，號慟入門，形容臒毀，妻不之識。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he wailed as he entered the gate; his appearance was emaciated and wasted, and his wife did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he wailed as he entered the gate. He was so emaciated and wasted that his wife did not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 後擢進士第。

translations.literal: Later he passed the highest tier of the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the jinshi examination at the highest tier.

sentences.zh: 天授中，再遷太子司議郎兼修國史、崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he was twice promoted to Secretary for Memorials to the Crown Prince, concurrently compiling the national history and serving as Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was twice promoted to Secretary for Memorials to the Crown Prince, while also compiling the national history and serving as Academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 數受詔纂輯慶恤儀典，武後稱之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received edicts to compile rites for felicitations and condolence, and Empress Wu praised his work.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly received edicts to compile rites for felicitations and condolence, and Empress Wu praised his work.

sentences.zh: 尤明姓系，自魏、晉以降，推本其來，皆有條序，著《姓略》、《衣冠系錄》等百餘篇。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in clan genealogy; from Wei and Jin downward he traced origins in orderly sequence, and authored more than a hundred works including Genealogical Summaries and Records of Official Families.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially expert in clan genealogy. From Wei and Jin downward he traced every lineage in orderly sequence, and wrote more than a hundred works, including Genealogical Summaries and Records of Official Families.

sentences.zh: 後坐綦連耀交通，下獄死。

translations.literal: Later he was implicated in dealings with Qi Lianyao, thrown into prison, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was later implicated in dealings with Qi Lianyao, thrown into prison, and died there.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he was posthumously awarded the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he was posthumously awarded the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弟敬潛，少與敬淳齊名，歷懷州錄事參軍，亦坐耀事系獄，免死。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jingqian in youth was as famous as Jingchun; he served as Recording Secretary of Huaizhou, and was also imprisoned on account of Lianyao's affair but escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jingqian was as renowned as Jingchun in their youth. He served as recording secretary of Huaizhou and was also imprisoned in Lianyao's affair, but escaped death.

sentences.zh: 後為遂安令。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Suian.
translations.idiomatic: He later became magistrate of Suian.

sentences.zh: 先是，令多死，敬潛欲辭，妻曰：「君不死獄而得全，非生死有命邪？」

translations.literal: Previously, many magistrates of that county had died; Jingqian wished to decline the appointment, but his wife said: "You escaped death in prison and were spared—is life and death not a matter of fate?"
translations.idiomatic: Previously many magistrates of that county had died. Jingqian wished to decline the appointment, but his wife said: "You escaped death in prison and were spared—is life and death not a matter of fate?

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: He agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 到官，有梟嘯其屏，鼠數十走於前，左右驅之，擁杖而號，敬潛不為懼。

translations.literal: Upon taking office, an owl shrieked at his screen and dozens of rats ran before him; his attendants drove them away, yet clutching his staff he wailed—and Jingqian was not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking office, an owl shrieked at his screen and dozens of rats scurried before him. His attendants drove them away, yet clutching his staff he wailed—and Jingqian was not afraid.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷衛令，位中書舍人。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to magistrate of Wei and held the post of Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to magistrate of Wei and held the post of Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 唐初，姓譜學唯敬淳名家。

translations.literal: In the early Tang, in the study of clan genealogies only Jingchun's family was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tang, only the Lu family of Jingchun was renowned in the study of clan genealogies.

sentences.zh: 其後柳沖、韋述、蕭穎士、孔至各有撰次，然皆本之路氏。

translations.literal: Afterward Liu Chong, Wei Shu, Xiao Yingshi, and Kong Zhi each compiled works of their own, yet all were based on the Lu clan's scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Chong, Wei Shu, Xiao Yingshi, and Kong Zhi each compiled works of their own, yet all drew on the Lu family's scholarship.

sentences.zh: 王元感，濮州鄄城人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuangan was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuangan came from Juancheng in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢明經高第，調博城丞。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination at the highest tier and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Bocheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination at the highest tier and was appointed assistant magistrate of Bocheng.

sentences.zh: 紀王慎為兗州都督，厚加禮，敕其子東平王續往受業。

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Ji was Military Governor of Yanzhou and treated him with great courtesy, ordering his son the Prince of Dongping to go and receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Ji was military governor of Yanzhou and treated him with great courtesy, ordering his son the Prince of Dongping to go and study under him.

sentences.zh: 天授中，稍遷左衛率府錄事，兼直弘文館。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he was gradually promoted to Recording Secretary of the Left Guard Office and concurrently served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was gradually promoted to recording secretary of the Left Guard Office while concurrently serving on duty at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 武後時，已郊，遂享明堂，封嵩山，詔與韋叔夏等草儀具，眾推其練洽。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, after the suburban sacrifice had been performed, the Bright Hall offering and Mount Song feng were carried out; he was ordered to draft the ritual provisions together with Wei Shuxia and others, and all praised his thorough mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, after the suburban sacrifice came the Bright Hall offering and the Mount Song feng; he was ordered to draft the ritual provisions with Wei Shuxia and others, and all praised his thorough mastery.

sentences.zh: 轉四門博士，仍直弘文館。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Four Gates and continued on duty at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Erudite of the Four Gates while continuing on duty at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 年雖老，讀書不廢夜。

translations.literal: Though advanced in years, he never ceased reading at night.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, he never stopped reading at night.

sentences.zh: 所撰《書糾謬》、《春秋振滯》、《禮繩愆》等凡數十百篇，長安時上之，丐官筆楮寫藏秘書。

translations.literal: The works he authored—including Corrections to the Documents, Resolving Difficulties in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Rectifying Errors in the Rites—numbered several tens to hundreds of chapters; during the Chang'an era he submitted them and begged for official paper and brushes to have them copied and stored in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Among the works he authored—Corrections to the Documents, Resolving Difficulties in the Spring and Autumn Annals, Rectifying Errors in the Rites, and others—were several tens to hundreds of chapters. During the Chang'an era he submitted them and begged for official paper and brushes to have them copied and stored in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有詔兩館學士、成均博士議可否。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the academicians of both halls and the Erudites of the Imperial Academy to debate their merits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the academicians of both halls and the Erudites of the Imperial Academy to debate their merits.

sentences.zh: 祝欽明、郭山惲、李憲等本章句家，見元感詆先儒同異，不懌，數沮詰其言，元感緣罅申釋，竟不詘。

translations.literal: Zhu Qinming, Guo Shanyun, Li Xian, and others were classicists of the commentarial school; seeing that Yuangan criticized the earlier Ru for their differences, they were displeased and repeatedly obstructed and challenged his words; Yuangan seized on gaps to explain, and in the end was not defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qinming, Guo Shanyun, Li Xian, and others were classicists of the commentarial school. Seeing that Yuangan criticized the earlier Ru for their disagreements, they were displeased and repeatedly obstructed and challenged him; Yuangan seized on openings to explain, and in the end was not defeated.

sentences.zh: 魏知古見其書，嘆曰：「《五經》指南也。」

translations.literal: Wei Zhigu saw his books and sighed: "A guide to the Five Classics."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu saw his books and sighed: "A guide to the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 而徐堅、劉知幾、張思敬等惜其異聞，每為助理，聯疏薦之，遂下詔褒美，以為儒宗。

translations.literal: Yet Xu Jian, Liu Zhiji, Zhang Sijing, and others valued his unusual findings and often assisted him; they jointly submitted a memorial recommending him, and an edict was issued praising him as a patriarch of the Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xu Jian, Liu Zhiji, Zhang Sijing, and others valued his unusual findings and often assisted him. They jointly submitted a memorial recommending him, and an edict was issued praising him as a patriarch of the Ru.

sentences.zh: 拜太子司議郎兼崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary for Memorials to the Crown Prince and concurrently Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretary for Memorials to the Crown Prince and concurrently Academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 中宗以東宮官屬，加朝散大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, on account of his service among the Eastern Palace officials, additionally granted him the honorary title of Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong, on account of his service among the Eastern Palace officials, additionally granted him the honorary title of Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and he died.

sentences.zh: 元感初著論三年之喪以三十有六月，譏詆諸儒。

translations.literal: Yuangan had initially authored a treatise arguing that the three-year mourning period should be thirty-six months, criticizing and denouncing the various Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangan had initially written a treatise arguing that the three-year mourning period should be thirty-six months, criticizing and denouncing the various Ru.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人張柬之破其說曰：「三年之喪，二十五月，由古則然。

translations.literal: Fengge Attendant Zhang Jianzhi refuted his argument, saying: "The three-year mourning period is twenty-five months; thus it has been since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Fengge Attendant Zhang Jianzhi refuted his argument, saying: "The three-year mourning period is twenty-five months; thus it has been since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》僖公三十三年十二月『乙巳，公薨』，文公二年冬『公子遂如齊納幣』。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, in the thirty-third year of Duke Xi, twelfth month, 'On the day yisi the Duke died'; in the second year of Duke Wen, winter, 'The Duke's son Sui went to Qi to deliver betrothal gifts.'
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the thirty-third year of Duke Xi, twelfth month, "On the day yisi the Duke died," and in the second year of Duke Wen, winter, "The Duke's son Sui went to Qi to deliver betrothal gifts."

sentences.zh: 左氏曰：『禮也。』

translations.literal: Zuo's Commentary says: 'This accorded with ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's Commentary says: "This accorded with ritual."

sentences.zh: 杜預謂：『僖喪終是年十一月，納幣在十二月。

translations.literal: Du Yu explained: 'Duke Xi's mourning ended in the eleventh month of that year; the betrothal gifts were delivered in the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu explained: "Duke Xi's mourning ended in the eleventh month of that year; the betrothal gifts were delivered in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 故謂之禮。』

translations.literal: Therefore it is called ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is called ritual.

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》：『納幣不書，此何以書？

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary asks: 'The delivery of betrothal gifts is not recorded—why is this recorded?
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary asks: "The delivery of betrothal gifts is not normally recorded—why is this recorded?

sentences.zh: 譏。

translations.literal: To censure.
translations.idiomatic: To censure.

sentences.zh: 何以譏？

translations.literal: Why censure?
translations.idiomatic: Why censure?

sentences.zh: 三年之內不圖婚。』

translations.literal: Within the three-year mourning period one must not plan marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Within the three-year mourning period one must not plan marriage.

sentences.zh: 何休曰：『僖以十二月薨，未終二十五月，故譏雲。』

translations.literal: He Xiu said: 'Duke Xi died in the twelfth month; the twenty-five months had not yet ended, and therefore it is censured.'
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu said: "Duke Xi died in the twelfth month; the twenty-five months had not yet ended, and therefore it is censured."

sentences.zh: 杜預推歷乙巳乃在十一月，《經》書十二月為誤。

translations.literal: Du Yu calculated the calendar and found that yisi fell in the eleventh month; the Classic's recording of the twelfth month was an error.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu calculated the calendar and found that yisi fell in the eleventh month; the Classic's recording of the twelfth month was an error.

sentences.zh: 文公元年四月，葬僖公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duke Wen, fourth month, Duke Xi was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duke Wen, fourth month, Duke Xi was buried.

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'Delayed.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "Delayed."

sentences.zh: 夫諸侯之葬五月，若十二月薨，五月不得雲緩，則十一月明甚。

translations.literal: The burial of a feudal lord takes place in the fifth month; if he died in the twelfth month, a fifth-month burial could not be called delayed—thus the eleventh month is clearly established.
translations.idiomatic: The burial of a feudal lord takes place in the fifth month; if he had died in the twelfth month, a fifth-month burial could not be called delayed—thus the eleventh month is clearly established.

sentences.zh: 然二家所競，乃一月，非一歲，則二十五月，其一驗也。

translations.literal: Yet what the two schools disputed was a single month, not a full year—thus twenty-five months is confirmed by one piece of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the two schools disputed was a single month, not a full year—thus twenty-five months is confirmed by one piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 《書》稱成湯既沒，太甲元年曰：『惟元祀，十有二月，伊尹祀於先王，奉嗣王祇見厥祖。』

translations.literal: The Documents states that after King Cheng Tang died, in the first year of Tai Jia it says: 'In the first year, twelfth month, Yi Yin sacrificed to the former king and presented the heir king to see his ancestors.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents states that after King Cheng Tang died, in the first year of Tai Jia it says: "In the first year, twelfth month, Yi Yin sacrificed to the former king and presented the heir king to see his ancestors."

sentences.zh: 孔安國曰：『湯以元年十一月崩。』

translations.literal: Kong Anguo said: 'Tang died in the eleventh month of the first year.'
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo said: "Tang died in the eleventh month of the first year."

sentences.zh: 此則明年祥，又明年大祥，故下言『惟三祀，十有二月朔，尹以冕服，奉嗣王歸於亳』。

translations.literal: This means that in the following year came xiang, and in the year after that da xiang; hence the next passage says 'In the third year, twelfth month, first day, Yi led the heir king in cap and robes back to Bo.'
translations.idiomatic: This means that in the following year came xiang, and in the year after that da xiang; hence the next passage says "In the third year, twelfth month, first day, Yi led the heir king in cap and robes back to Bo."

sentences.zh: 是十一月服除而冕。

translations.literal: Thus in the eleventh month the mourning garments were removed and the cap was worn.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the eleventh month the mourning garments were removed and the cap was worn.

sentences.zh: 《顧命》：『四月哉生魄，王不懌。

translations.literal: The Announcement of the Testamentary Charge says: 'In the fourth month, on the day when the moon was first waxing, the king was displeased.'
translations.idiomatic: The Announcement of the Testamentary Charge says: "In the fourth month, on the day when the moon was first waxing, the king was displeased."

sentences.zh: 翌日乙丑，王崩。

translations.literal: The next day, yichou, the king died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, yichou, the king died.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，命作冊度。

translations.literal: On dingmao he ordered the preparation of the written ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he ordered the preparation of the written ordinances.

sentences.zh: 越七日癸酉，伯相命士須材。』

translations.literal: Seven days later, on guiyou, the chief minister ordered the officers to prepare the materials.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later, on guiyou, the chief minister ordered the officers to prepare the materials.

sentences.zh: 則成王崩至康王麻冕黼裳凡十日，康王始見廟。

translations.literal: Thus from King Cheng's death until King Kang wore the hemp cap and skirt with embroidered hem was altogether ten days; only then did King Kang first visit the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from King Cheng's death until King Kang wore the hemp cap and skirt with embroidered hem was ten days in all; only then did King Kang first visit the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 明湯崩在十一月。

translations.literal: Clearly Tang died in the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly Tang died in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 比殯訖，以十二月祗見其祖。

translations.literal: When the encoffining was finished, in the twelfth month he reverently visited his ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When the encoffining was complete, in the twelfth month he reverently presented himself before his ancestor.

sentences.zh: 《顧命》見廟訖『諸侯出廟門俟』，《伊訓》言『祗見厥祖，侯甸群後鹹在』，則崩及見廟，周因於殷也，非元年前復有一歲，此二十五月之二驗。

translations.literal: The Announcement of the Testamentary Charge, after the temple visit was finished, says 'The feudal lords went out the temple gate and waited'; the Instructions of Yi says 'He reverently visited his ancestor, and the marquises, the domain lords, and all the host of nobles were present'—thus from death to the temple visit, Zhou followed Yin; it is not that there was another full year before the first year—this is the second proof of twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: The Announcement of the Testamentary Charge, once the temple visit was finished, says, "The feudal lords went out the temple gate and waited"; the Instructions of Yi says, "He reverently visited his ancestor, and the marquises, domain lords, and all the host of nobles were present." Thus from death to the temple visit, Zhou followed Yin; it is not that another full year intervened before the first year—this is the second proof of twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：『三年之喪，二十五月而畢，哀痛未盡，然而以是為斷者，送死有已，服生有節。』

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: 'The three-year mourning is completed in twenty-five months; though grief is not yet exhausted, yet to take this as the limit is because sending off the dead has its end, and serving the living has its measure.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: "The three-year mourning is completed in twenty-five months; though grief is not yet exhausted, yet to take this as the limit is because sending off the dead has its end, and serving the living has its measure.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『期而小祥，食菜果；

translations.literal: It also says: 'After one year comes xiao xiang, and one eats vegetables and fruit;
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "After one year comes xiao xiang, and one eats vegetables and fruit;

sentences.zh: 又期而大祥，有醯醬；

translations.literal: After another year comes da xiang, and there are pickles and sauces;
translations.idiomatic: After another year comes da xiang, and there are pickles and sauces;

sentences.zh: 中月而禫，食酒肉。』

translations.literal: In the middle month comes tan, and one eats wine and meat.'
translations.idiomatic: In the middle month comes tan, and one eats wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『再期之喪，三年；

translations.literal: It also says: 'Mourning of two periods is three years;
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Mourning of two periods is three years;

sentences.zh: 期之喪，二年；

translations.literal: Mourning of one period is two years;
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of one period is two years;

sentences.zh: 九月、七月之喪，三時；

translations.literal: Mourning of nine months or seven months is three seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of nine months or seven months is three seasons;

sentences.zh: 五月之喪，二時；

translations.literal: Mourning of five months is two seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of five months is two seasons;

sentences.zh: 三月之喪，一時。』

translations.literal: Mourning of three months is one season.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of three months is one season.

sentences.zh: 此二十五月之三驗。

translations.literal: This is the third proof of twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third proof of twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 《儀禮》：『期而小祥，又期而大祥，中月而禫，是月也，吉祭。』

translations.literal: The Ceremonies says: 'After one period comes xiao xiang; after another period comes da xiang; in the middle month comes tan—in that month, auspicious sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonies says: "After one period comes xiao xiang; after another period comes da xiang; in the middle month comes tan—in that month, auspicious sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 此二十五月之四驗。

translations.literal: This is the fourth proof of twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth proof of twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 《書》、《春秋》、《禮》皆周公、尼父所定，敢問此可為法否？

translations.literal: The Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Rites were all established by the Duke of Zhou and the Master—dare I ask whether this may be taken as law?
translations.idiomatic: The Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Rites were all established by the Duke of Zhou and Confucius—dare I ask whether this may be taken as law?

sentences.zh: 昔鄭玄以中月而禫者，內容一月，自喪至禫，凡二十七月。

translations.literal: Formerly Zheng Xuan held that 'in the middle month comes tan' included a full month within it, so from mourning to tan was altogether twenty-seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zheng Xuan held that "in the middle month comes tan" included a full month within it, so from mourning to tan was altogether twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 今既用之，而二十五月初無疑論。

translations.literal: Now that this has been adopted, at the beginning of the twenty-fifth month there was no dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Now that this has been adopted, at the beginning of the twenty-fifth month there was no dispute.

sentences.zh: 大抵子於親喪，有終身之痛，創巨者日久，痛深者愈遲，何歲月而止乎？

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, a son in mourning for a parent has pain that lasts a lifetime; the greater the wound, the longer the days; the deeper the grief, the slower the recovery—how could one stop at a fixed number of months?
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, a son mourning a parent carries pain that lasts a lifetime; the greater the wound, the longer the days; the deeper the grief, the slower the recovery—how could one stop at a fixed number of months?

sentences.zh: 故練而慨然，悲慕未盡，而踴擗之情差未；

translations.literal: Thus at lian one sighs deeply, for longing and grief are not yet exhausted, and the feeling of stamping and beating one's breast is not yet diminished;
translations.idiomatic: Thus at lian one sighs deeply, for longing and grief are not yet exhausted, and the impulse to stamp and beat one's breast is not yet diminished;

sentences.zh: 祥而廓然，哀傷已除，而孤藐之懷更劇。

translations.literal: At xiang one grows calm, for sorrow and injury have been removed, yet the feeling of orphanhood grows keener.
translations.idiomatic: At xiang one grows calm, for sorrow and injury have been removed, yet the feeling of orphanhood grows keener.

sentences.zh: 此情之所致，寧外飾哉？

translations.literal: This is what feeling brings about—could it be merely outward display?
translations.idiomatic: This is what feeling brings about—could it be merely outward display?

sentences.zh: 故先王立其中制，使情文兩稱，是以祥則縞帶素紕，禫則無不佩。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings established a mean measure, so that feeling and form would both be fitting; thus at xiang one wears the white headband and white edge, and at tan one always wears ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former kings established a mean measure, so that feeling and form would both be fitting; thus at xiang one wears the white headband and white edge, and at tan one always wears ornaments.

sentences.zh: 夫去衰麻，襲錦縠，行道之人皆不忍，直為節之以禮，叵如之何。

translations.literal: To remove the hemp mourning garments and put on brocade and gauze—even passersby on the road cannot bear it; it is simply that ritual sets bounds to it—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: To remove the hemp mourning garments and put on brocade and gauze—even passersby on the road cannot bear it; it is simply that ritual sets bounds to it—what can be done?

sentences.zh: 故仲由不能過制為姊服，孔鯉不能過期哭母，彼詎不懷？

translations.literal: Thus Zhong You could not exceed the measure in mourning for his elder sister, and Kong Li could not mourn his mother beyond the prescribed period—did they not feel grief?
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhong You could not exceed the measure in mourning for his elder sister, and Kong Li could not mourn his mother beyond the prescribed period—did they not feel grief?

sentences.zh: 畏名教之嚴也。」

translations.literal: They feared the strictness of the teaching of names and relationships.
translations.idiomatic: They feared the strictness of the teaching of names and relationships.

sentences.zh: 當世謂柬之言不詭聖人，而元感論遂廢。

translations.literal: Contemporaries held that Jianzhi's words did not pervert the sages, and Yuangan's treatise was thereupon abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held that Jianzhi's words did not pervert the sages, and Yuangan's treatise was thereupon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 王紹宗，字承烈，梁左民尚書銓曾孫。

translations.literal: Wang Shaozong, courtesy name Chenglie, was a great-grandson of Quan, Left Minister of the People of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaozong, courtesy name Chenglie, was a great-grandson of Quan, Left Minister of the People under Liang.

sentences.zh: 系本瑯邪，徙江都雲。

translations.literal: His lineage originated in Langye; they migrated to Yun in Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: His lineage originated in Langye; the family migrated to Yun in Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 少貧俠，嗜學，工草隸，客居僧坊，寫書取庸自給，凡三十年。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor but chivalrous, devoted to learning, and skilled in cursive and clerical script; he lodged in a monks' quarters, copying books for wages to support himself—for thirty years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was poor but chivalrous, devoted to learning, and skilled in cursive and clerical script; he lodged in a monks' quarters, copying books for wages to support himself—for thirty years in all.

sentences.zh: 庸足給一月即止，不取贏，人雖厚償，輒拒不受。

translations.literal: When his wages sufficed for one month he would stop, taking no surplus; though people offered generous payment, he always refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When his wages sufficed for one month he would stop, taking no surplus; though people offered generous payment, he always refused and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業起兵，聞其行，以幣劫之，稱疾篤。

translations.literal: When Xu Jingye raised troops, hearing of his conduct, he sent gifts to coerce him; Shaozong claimed grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingye raised troops, hearing of his conduct, he sent gifts to coerce him into service; Shaozong claimed grave illness.

sentences.zh: 復令唐之奇強遣，不肯赴，敬業怒，將殺之，之奇曰：「彼人望也，殺之沮士心，不可。」

translations.literal: Jingye again had Tang Zhiqi forcibly dispatch him, but he refused to go; Jingye was angry and was about to kill him. Zhiqi said: "That man has public esteem; to kill him would dampen the soldiers' hearts—it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye again had Tang Zhiqi forcibly dispatch him, but he refused to go; Jingye was angry and was about to kill him. Zhiqi said: "That man has public esteem; to kill him would dampen the soldiers' hearts—it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 由是免。

translations.literal: Thus he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he was spared.

sentences.zh: 事平，大總管李孝逸表其節，武後召赴東都，謁殿中，褒慰良厚，擢太子文學。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Grand General of Pacification Li Xiaoyi memorialized his integrity; Empress Wu summoned him to the Eastern Capital, and when he was received in the palace hall she praised and comforted him generously, promoting him to Literary Scholar of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Grand General of Pacification Li Xiaoyi memorialized his integrity; Empress Wu summoned him to the Eastern Capital, and when he was received in the palace hall she praised and comforted him generously, promoting him to Literary Scholar of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 累進秘書少監，使侍皇太子。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat and was assigned to attend the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat and was assigned to attend the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 紹宗雅修飾，當時公卿莫不慕悅其風，張易之兄弟亦頗結納。

translations.literal: Shaozong was refined in personal adornment; at the time none among the high ministers and nobles did not admire and delight in his manner, and the brothers Zhang Yizhi also cultivated ties with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong was refined in personal adornment; at the time none among the high ministers and nobles failed to admire and delight in his manner, and the brothers Zhang Yizhi also cultivated ties with him.

sentences.zh: 易之誅，坐廢，卒於家。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, Shaozong was implicated and dismissed; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi was executed, Shaozong was implicated and dismissed; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 嘗與人書曰：「鄙夫書無工者，特由水墨之積習耳。

translations.literal: He once wrote to someone: "A vulgar man's writing has no skill—it is simply the accumulated habit of ink and water.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to someone: "A vulgar man's writing has no skill—it is simply the accumulated habit of ink and water.

sentences.zh: 常精心率意、虛神靜思以取之。

translations.literal: One must constantly concentrate the mind, follow one's intent, empty the spirit, and quiet one's thoughts to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: One must constantly concentrate the mind, follow one's intent, empty the spirit, and quiet one's thoughts to obtain it.

sentences.zh: 吳中陸大夫常以余比虞君，以不臨寫故也。

translations.literal: Grand Master Lu of Wu often compared me to Lord Yu—because I do not copy from models.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Lu of Wu often compared me to Lord Yu—because I do not copy from models.

sentences.zh: 聞虞被中畫腹，與余正同。」

translations.literal: I heard that Yu, while under the covers, would draw on his belly—the same as my own practice.
translations.idiomatic: I heard that Yu, while under the covers, would draw on his belly—the same as my own practice.

sentences.zh: 虞，即世南也。

translations.literal: Yu was Yu Shinan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was Yu Shinan.

sentences.zh: 紹宗兄玄宗，隱嵩山，號太和先生，傳黃老術。

translations.literal: Shaozong's elder brother Xuanzong hid himself on Mount Song, styled himself Master of Grand Harmony, and transmitted the arts of Huang-Lao.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong's elder brother Xuanzong hid himself on Mount Song, styled himself Master of Grand Harmony, and transmitted the arts of Huang-Lao.

sentences.zh: 彭景直，瀛州河間人。

translations.literal: Peng Jingzhi was a man of Hejian in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Jingzhi was a man of Hejian in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 中宗景龍末，為太常博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jinglong era of Emperor Zhongzong, he served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jinglong era of Emperor Zhongzong, he served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時獻、昭、乾三陵皆日祭，景直上言：在禮，陵不日祭，宗廟有月祭，故王者設廟、祧、壇、
