translations.literal: At that time the tombs of Xian, Zhao, and Qian all received daily sacrifice; Jingzhi submitted a memorial: according to ritual, tombs are not sacrificed to daily; ancestral temples receive monthly sacrifice—therefore kings establish temples, tiao, altars,
translations.idiomatic: At that time the tombs of Xian, Zhao, and Qian all received daily sacrifice; Jingzhi submitted a memorial: according to ritual, tombs are not sacrificed to daily; ancestral temples receive monthly sacrifice—therefore kings establish temples, tiao, altars,

sentences.zh: 墠，為親疏多少之殺。

translations.literal: and open-air platforms, according to the gradations of closeness and distance.
translations.idiomatic: and open-air platforms, according to the gradations of closeness and distance.

sentences.zh: 立七廟、一壇、一墠。

translations.literal: They establish seven temples, one altar, and one open-air platform.
translations.idiomatic: They establish seven temples, one altar, and one open-air platform.

sentences.zh: 曰考廟，曰王考廟，曰皇考廟，曰顯考廟，皆月祭。

translations.literal: There is the temple of the father, the temple of the grandfather, the temple of the great-grandfather, and the temple of the remote ancestor—all receive monthly sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: There is the temple of the father, the temple of the grandfather, the temple of the great-grandfather, and the temple of the remote ancestor—all receive monthly sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 遠廟為祧，享嘗乃止。

translations.literal: Remote temples become tiao; offering and tasting sacrifice then cease.
translations.idiomatic: Remote temples become tiao; offering and tasting sacrifice then cease.

sentences.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱祭之，無禱乃止。

translations.literal: When tiao are removed they become altars; when altars are removed they become open-air platforms; when there is prayer sacrifice they are served; when there is no prayer they cease.
translations.idiomatic: When tiao are removed they become altars; when altars are removed they become open-air platforms; when there is prayer sacrifice they are served; when there is no prayer they cease.

sentences.zh: 譙周曰：「天子始祖、高祖、曾祖、祖、考之廟，皆朔加薦，以象生時朔食，號月祭，二祧廟不月祭。」

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou said: "The temples of the Son of Heaven's founding ancestor, high ancestor, great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father all receive offerings on the first of the month, imitating the morning meal of life—this is called monthly sacrifice; the two tiao temples do not receive monthly sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou said: "The temples of the Son of Heaven's founding ancestor, high ancestor, great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father all receive offerings on the first of the month, imitating the morning meal of life—this is called monthly sacrifice; the two tiao temples do not receive monthly sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 則古無日祭者。

translations.literal: Thus in antiquity there was no daily sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in antiquity there was no daily sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今諸陵朔、望進食，近古之殷事；

translations.literal: Now at the various tombs offerings are presented on the first and fifteenth of the month—this approximates the Yin practice of antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: Now at the various tombs offerings are presented on the first and fifteenth of the month—this approximates the Yin practice of antiquity;

sentences.zh: 諸節進食，近古之薦新。

translations.literal: offerings presented at the various festivals approximate the offering of new produce of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: offerings presented at the various festivals approximate the offering of new produce of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：「殷事，月之朔、半，薦新奠也。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Yin practice means on the first and middle of the month, offering new produce as sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said: "Yin practice means on the first and middle of the month, offering new produce as sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 於《儀禮》，朔、半日，猶常日朝夕也，既大祥，即四時焉，此其祭皆在廟雲。

translations.literal: In the Ceremonies, on the first and middle days of the month one still observes the regular morning and evening rites; after da xiang, then come the four seasons—yet these sacrifices are all in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ceremonies, on the first and middle days of the month one still observes the regular morning and evening rites; after da xiang, then come the four seasons—yet these sacrifices are all in the temple.

sentences.zh: 近世始以朔、望諸節祭陵寢，唯四時及臘，五享於廟。

translations.literal: In recent times people began to sacrifice at tomb chambers on the first, fifteenth, and various festival days; only at the four seasons and at la are the five offerings made in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times people began to sacrifice at tomb chambers on the first, fifteenth, and various festival days; only at the four seasons and at la are the five offerings made in the temple.

sentences.zh: 尋經質禮，無日祭於陵之文。

translations.literal: Searching the classics and examining ritual, there is no text authorizing daily sacrifice at tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Searching the classics and examining ritual, there is no text authorizing daily sacrifice at tombs.

sentences.zh: 漢時，京師自高祖下至宣帝，與太上皇、悼皇考陵旁立廟。

translations.literal: In Han times, from the capital from Gaozu down to Emperor Xuan, together with the tombs of the Grand Supreme Emperor and the Lamented Imperial Father, temples were erected beside the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, in the capital from Gaozu down to Emperor Xuan, together with the tombs of the Grand Supreme Emperor and the Lamented Imperial Father, temples were erected beside the tombs.

sentences.zh: 園各有寢、便殿，故日祭諸寢，月祭諸便殿。

translations.literal: Each park had its sleeping chamber and convenience hall; therefore daily sacrifice was at the various sleeping chambers, and monthly sacrifice at the various convenience halls.
translations.idiomatic: Each park had its sleeping chamber and convenience hall; therefore daily sacrifice was at the various sleeping chambers, and monthly sacrifice at the various convenience halls.

sentences.zh: 貢禹以禮節煩數，白元帝願罷郡、國廟。

translations.literal: Gong Yu, because the rites were excessively numerous, reported to Emperor Yuan asking that the district and state temples be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yu, because the rites were excessively numerous, reported to Emperor Yuan asking that the district and state temples be abolished.

sentences.zh: 丞相韋玄成等後因議七廟外寢園皆無復修。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wei Xuancheng and others later, in their deliberations, likewise ceased all further repair of the outer sleeping parks beyond the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wei Xuancheng and others later, in their deliberations, likewise ceased all further repair of the outer sleeping parks beyond the seven temples.

sentences.zh: 議者亦以祭不欲數，宜復古四時祭於廟。

translations.literal: Those deliberating also held that sacrifice should not be too frequent, and that one should restore the ancient practice of four-season sacrifice in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Those deliberating also held that sacrifice should not be too frequent, and that one should restore the ancient practice of four-season sacrifice in the temple.

sentences.zh: 劉歆引《春秋外傳》曰：「祖、禰日祭，曾、高月祀，二祧時享，壇、墠歲貢。」

translations.literal: Liu Xin cited the Outer Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Ancestor and immediate forebear receive daily sacrifice; great-great-grandfather and great-grandfather receive monthly sacrifice; the two tiao receive seasonal offering; altars and open-air platforms receive yearly tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin cited the Outer Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Ancestor and immediate forebear receive daily sacrifice; great-great-grandfather and great-grandfather receive monthly sacrifice; the two tiao receive seasonal offering; altars and open-air platforms receive yearly tribute.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以降，不祭墓。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, graves were not sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, graves were not sacrificed to.

sentences.zh: 唐家擇古作法，臣謂宜罷諸陵日祭，如禮便。

translations.literal: Our Tang dynasty selects ancient practice and follows it; your servant holds that daily sacrifice at the various tombs should be abolished, as ritual requires.
translations.idiomatic: Our Tang dynasty selects ancient practice and follows it; your servant holds that daily sacrifice at the various tombs should be abolished, as ritual requires.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，因下詔：「有司言諸陵不當日進食。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree, and thereupon issued an edict: "The responsible officials say the various tombs ought not receive daily offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree, and thereupon issued an edict: "The responsible officials say the various tombs ought not receive daily offerings.

sentences.zh: 夫禮以人情為之沿革，何專古而泥所聞？

translations.literal: Ritual follows human feeling in its changes and continuations—why adhere exclusively to antiquity and cling to what one has heard?
translations.idiomatic: Ritual follows human feeling in its changes and continuations—why adhere exclusively to antiquity and cling to what one has heard?

sentences.zh: 乾陵宜朝晡進奠，昭、獻陵日一進，或所司乏於費，可減朕常膳為之。」

translations.literal: At Qianling offerings should be presented morning and afternoon; at Zhao and Xian tombs one offering per day—or if the responsible offices lack funds, my regular meals may be reduced to provide for it."
translations.idiomatic: At Qianling offerings should be presented morning and afternoon; at Zhao and Xian tombs one offering per day—or if the responsible offices lack funds, my regular meals may be reduced to provide for it."

sentences.zh: 帝崩，葬定陵，有司議以和思皇后祔葬，後為武後所殺，不得其喪所，將以招魂合諸梓宮，景直曰：「招魂古無傳，不可。

translations.literal: When the emperor died and was buried at Dingling, the responsible officials deliberated associating in burial Empress Hexi, who had later been killed by Empress Wu and whose place of burial could not be found; they were about to summon the soul and unite it with the inner coffin. Jingzhi said: "Summoning the soul has no precedent in antiquity—it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died and was buried at Dingling, the responsible officials deliberated associating in burial Empress Hexi, who had later been killed by Empress Wu and whose place of burial could not be found; they were about to summon the soul and unite it with the inner coffin. Jingzhi said: "Summoning the soul has no precedent in antiquity—it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 請如橋山藏衣冠故事，納後祎衣，復寢宮，舉衣魂輅，告以太牢，內之方中，奉帝梓棺右，覆以夷衾。」

translations.literal: I ask that we follow the precedent of burying robes and caps at Qiao Mountain: place the empress's ceremonial robe within, restore the sleeping chamber, raise the robe on the soul carriage, announce it with the grand sacrifice, place it within the square enclosure, set it to the right of the emperor's inner coffin, and cover it with the plain quilt.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we follow the precedent of burying robes and caps at Qiao Mountain: place the empress's ceremonial robe within, restore the sleeping chamber, raise the robe on the soul carriage, announce it with the grand sacrifice, place it within the square enclosure, set it to the right of the emperor's inner coffin, and cover it with the plain quilt.

sentences.zh: 眾當其言，制曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The assembly approved his proposal; the decree said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly approved his proposal; the decree said: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 景直後歷禮部郎中卒。

translations.literal: Jingzhi later served as Director in the Ministry of Rites and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi later served as Director in the Ministry of Rites and died in office.

sentences.zh: 盧粲，幽州范陽人，後魏侍中陽烏五世孫。

translations.literal: Lu Can was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou, a fifth-generation descendant of Attendant-in-Ordinary Yangwu of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Can was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou, a fifth-generation descendant of Attendant-in-Ordinary Yangwu of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖彥卿，亦善著書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanqing was also skilled at writing books.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanqing was also skilled at writing books.

sentences.zh: 粲始冠，擢進士第。

translations.literal: When Can first came of age, he was selected in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Can first came of age, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era he was promoted in succession to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was promoted in succession to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時節湣太子立，韋後疾之，諷中宗以衛府封物給東宮，粲駁奏：「太子匕鬯主，歲時服用，宜取於百司。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince of Min was established; Empress Wei resented it and prompted Emperor Zhongzong to grant the Eastern Palace sealed goods from the guard offices. Can submitted a rebuttal: "The heir apparent's sacrificial vessels and annual and seasonal supplies should be taken from the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Crown Prince of Min was established; Empress Wei resented it and prompted Emperor Zhongzong to grant the Eastern Palace sealed goods from the guard offices. Can submitted a rebuttal: "The heir apparent's sacrificial vessels and annual and seasonal supplies should be taken from the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》：諸用財器，『歲終則會，唯王及太子不會』。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: for all uses of wealth and vessels, 'at year's end there is reckoning—only the king and the heir apparent are not reckoned.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou: for all uses of wealth and vessels, "at year's end there is reckoning—only the king and the heir apparent are not reckoned."

sentences.zh: 今乃與諸王等夷，非所謂憲章古昔者。」

translations.literal: Now to treat him the same as the various princes is not what is meant by taking the ancient statutes as model.
translations.idiomatic: Now to treat him the same as the various princes is not what is meant by taking the ancient statutes as model.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 武崇訓死，詔墓視陵制，粲曰：「凡王、公主墓，無稱陵者，唯永泰公主事出特制，非後人所援比。

translations.literal: When Wu Chongxun died, an edict ordered his tomb to follow tomb regulations. Can said: "For tombs of kings and princesses in general there is no designation of ling; only Princess Yongtai received a special decree—later men should not cite it as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Chongxun died, an edict ordered his tomb to follow tomb regulations. Can said: "For tombs of kings and princesses in general there is no designation of ling; only Princess Yongtai received a special decree—later men should not cite it as precedent.

sentences.zh: 崇訓塋兆，請視諸王。」

translations.literal: For Chongxun's tomb mound, I ask that it follow the standard for the various princes.
translations.idiomatic: For Chongxun's tomb mound, I ask that it follow the standard for the various princes.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「安樂公主與永泰不異，崇訓於主當同穴，為陵不疑。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Princess Anle differs not from Yongtai; Chongxun, as the princess's consort, should share her tomb—there is no doubt he should be a ling.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Princess Anle differs not from Yongtai; Chongxun, as the princess's consort, should share her tomb—there is no doubt he should be a ling.

sentences.zh: 粲固執，以「陵之稱，本施尊極，雖崇訓之親，不及雍王，雍墓不稱陵，崇訓緣主而得假是名哉？」

translations.literal: Can firmly persisted: "The designation ling is originally applied to the most exalted; though Chongxun was close in kinship, he did not equal Prince Yong—Yong's tomb was not called a ling; could Chongxun borrow that name through the princess?
translations.idiomatic: Can firmly persisted: "The designation ling is originally applied to the most exalted; though Chongxun was close in kinship, he did not equal Prince Yong—Yong's tomb was not called a ling; could Chongxun borrow that name through the princess?

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 主大怒，出粲陳州刺史。

translations.literal: The princess was greatly angered and had Can sent out as Prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was greatly angered and had Can sent out as Prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「茍所論得行，雖遠何憚！」

translations.literal: Can said: "If what I argued can be carried out, though distant I have no fear!
translations.idiomatic: Can said: "If what I argued can be carried out, though distant I have no fear!

sentences.zh: 開元初，為秘書少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其從父行嘉，仕為雍王記室，亦以學聞。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Xingjia served as Recorder of Prince Yong and was also known for learning.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Xingjia served as Recorder of Prince Yong and was also known for learning.

sentences.zh: 粲累封固安縣侯，終邠王傅，謚曰景。

translations.literal: Can was enfeoffed in succession as Marquis of Gu'an County, ended as Tutor to the Prince of Bin, and was posthumously titled Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Can was enfeoffed in succession as Marquis of Gu'an County, ended as Tutor to the Prince of Bin, and was posthumously titled Jing.

sentences.zh: 尹知章，絳州翼城人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhizhang was a man of Yicheng in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhizhang was a man of Yicheng in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少雖學，未甚通解，忽夢人持巨鑿破其心，內若劑焉，驚悟，誌思開徹，遂遍明《六經》。

translations.literal: In youth, though he studied, he had not attained thorough understanding; suddenly he dreamed that a man held a great chisel and broke open his heart—inside it was like medicine; startled awake, his thoughts opened and became penetrating, and he thereupon mastered the Six Classics completely.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, though he studied, he had not attained thorough understanding; suddenly he dreamed that a man held a great chisel and broke open his heart—inside it was like medicine; startled awake, his thoughts opened and became penetrating, and he thereupon mastered the Six Classics completely.

sentences.zh: 諸生嘗講授者，更北面受大義。

translations.literal: Those students who had formerly lectured to him turned to face north and received the great meaning from him.
translations.idiomatic: Those students who had formerly lectured to him turned to face north and received the great meaning from him.

sentences.zh: 長安中，擢定王府文學。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he was selected as Literary Scholar of the Prince of Ding's household.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he was selected as Literary Scholar of the Prince of Ding's household.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，或建言以涼武昭王為七廟始祖，知章議：「武昭遠世，非王業所因。」

translations.literal: During the Zhongzong era, some proposed making Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor of the seven temples; Zhizhang argued: "Wuzhao was of a remote age and was not the source from which royal enterprise arose."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhongzong era, some proposed making Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor of the seven temples; Zhizhang argued: "Wuzhao was of a remote age and was not the source from which royal enterprise arose.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: and the proposal was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 出為陸渾令，坐事，輒棄官去。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as magistrate of Luhun; implicated in an affair, he forthwith abandoned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Luhun, but when he became implicated in a matter, he immediately resigned and left office.

sentences.zh: 時散騎常侍解琬亦罷歸，與知章潭思經術，舉欣欣然。

translations.literal: At that time Attendant Cavalier-at-Large Xie Wan had also been dismissed and returned home; with Zhizhang they deeply contemplated the arts of the classics, and in all matters they were cheerfully content.
translations.idiomatic: About then Attendant Cavalier-at-Large Xie Wan was also dismissed and returned home; he and Zhizhang immersed themselves in classical learning, and their lives together were full of quiet contentment.

sentences.zh: 張說表諸朝，擢禮部員外郎，轉國子博士。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue presented a memorial to the court recommending him, and he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, then transferred to Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Yue's recommendation to the throne, he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Rites and later appointed erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 馬懷素緒定秘書，奏知章是正文字。

translations.literal: Ma Huaisu systematically organized the palace archives and submitted a memorial appointing Zhizhang to correct the orthography of texts.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Huaisu undertook to organize the palace archives, he recommended Zhizhang to standardize the written characters.

sentences.zh: 每休沐，講授未始輟。

translations.literal: On every day of mandated rest, his lecturing and instruction never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Even on his days off, he never stopped teaching.

sentences.zh: 於《易》、《老》、《莊》書尤縣解。

translations.literal: On the books of the Changes, the Laozi, and the Zhuangzi he was especially able to resolve all suspended doubts.
translations.idiomatic: He had an especially lucid grasp of the Book of Changes, the Laozi, and the Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 弟子貧者，赒給之。

translations.literal: When disciples were poor, he gave them relief.
translations.idiomatic: He supported students who could not afford to study on their own.

sentences.zh: 性和厚，人不見有喜慍。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and generous; people never saw him show joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: Mild and steady by nature, he never let pleasure or irritation show on his face.

sentences.zh: 未嘗問產業，其子欲廣市樵米為歲中計，知章曰：「如而計，則貧人何以取資？

translations.literal: He never inquired about property; his son wished to expand the buying and selling of firewood and grain as a plan for the year's income, and Zhizhang said: "If one calculates as you do, then by what means will poor people support themselves?
translations.idiomatic: He never concerned himself with the family fortune; when his son proposed buying up firewood and grain in bulk as a year's investment, Zhizhang said, "If we did as you suggest, how would the poor earn their living?

sentences.zh: 且吾尚應奪民利邪？」

translations.literal: Moreover, should I still be one to seize profit from the people?
translations.idiomatic: And would I really profit at the people's expense?

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 所註傳頗多，行於時。

translations.literal: The commentaries and expository works he annotated were quite numerous and circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He produced many commentaries and expository works, all widely read in his day.

sentences.zh: 門人孫季良等頌其德，刻著東都國子監門外。

translations.literal: His disciples, Sun Jiliang and others, praised his virtue and had it carved and set outside the gate of the Directorate of Education in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples including Sun Jiliang composed encomiums to his virtue and had them carved on stone outside the Directorate of Education in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 季良，偃師人，一名翌，仕歷左拾遺、集賢院直學士。

translations.literal: Jiliang was a man of Yanshi, with another name Yi; in office he rose through Reminder of the Left and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Jiliang, also called Yi, was a native of Yanshi who served as a left reminder and direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 張齊賢，陜州陜人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qixian was a man of Shan in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qixian was a native of Shan in Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，為太常奉禮郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengli era he served as Master of Ceremonies in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shengli reign he was appointed master of ceremonies in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 武後詔百官議告朔於明堂，讀時令，布政事，京官九品以上、四方朝集使皆列於廷。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered the hundred officials to discuss announcing the new moon at the Bright Hall, reading the seasonal ordinances, and promulgating government affairs; officials of the capital from the ninth rank upward and envoys of regional assemblies from the four quarters all took rank in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned the officials to debate performing the monthly announcement of the new moon at the Bright Hall, reading the seasonal ordinances, and issuing government business. Capital officials of the ninth rank and above, together with assembly envoys from the provinces, all lined the hall.

sentences.zh: 太常博士辟閭仁谞曰：「經無天子月告朔。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Pilü Renxu said: "The classics contain no instance of the Son of Heaven announcing the new moon every month.
translations.idiomatic: Pilü Renxu, erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, argued: "No classic text prescribes a monthly new-moon announcement for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 唯《玉藻》：『天子聽朔南門之外。』

translations.literal: Only the "Jade Regalia" states: "The Son of Heaven receives the new moon outside the southern gate."
translations.idiomatic: Only the "Jade Regalia" passage reads: "The Son of Heaven receives the new moon outside the southern gate."

sentences.zh: 《周太宰》：『正月之吉，布政於邦國都鄙。』

translations.literal: The "Grand Steward" chapter states: "On the auspicious day of the first month, promulgate government throughout the states, capitals, and districts."
translations.idiomatic: The "Grand Steward" chapter says: "On the auspicious day of the first month, promulgate government throughout the states, capitals, and districts."

sentences.zh: 幹寶曰：『建子月告朔日也。』

translations.literal: Gan Bao says: "The day of announcing the new moon in the first month of the jianzi cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao explains: "This refers to the new-moon day of the first month.

sentences.zh: 此《玉藻》聽朔同誼。

translations.literal: This accords with the meaning of "receiving the new moon" in the "Jade Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: This is the same in meaning as "receiving the new moon" in the "Jade Regalia.

sentences.zh: 今元日讀時令，合古聽朔事。

translations.literal: Now, reading the seasonal ordinances on New Year's Day conforms to the ancient practice of receiving the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the seasonal ordinances on New Year's Day, as we do now, matches the ancient rite of receiving the new moon.

sentences.zh: 獨鄭玄以秦制《月令》有五帝五官，因言『聽朔必以特牲告時帝及神，以文王、武王配。』

translations.literal: Only Zheng Xuan, following the Qin system of the "Monthly Ordinances" with its Five Emperors and Five Officials, further said: "In receiving the new moon one must use a special sacrificial victim to announce to the seasonal emperor and the spirits, with King Wen and King Wu as associates.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zheng Xuan, drawing on the Qin "Monthly Ordinances" with its Five Emperors and Five Officials, added that receiving the new moon required a special victim to announce to the seasonal emperor and the spirits, with King Wen and King Wu as associates.

sentences.zh: 其言非是。

translations.literal: That statement is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: That interpretation is wrong.

sentences.zh: 《月令》曰『其帝太昊，其神句芒』，謂宣令告人，使奉時務業，月皆有令，故云，非天子月朔以配帝祭也。

translations.literal: The "Monthly Ordinances" says "Its emperor is Taihao; its spirit is Goumang"—meaning to proclaim the ordinance and instruct people to observe the seasonal tasks and occupations; each month has its ordinance, hence the wording—it is not that the Son of Heaven announces the new moon each month to match emperors in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the "Monthly Ordinances" says "Its emperor is Taihao; its spirit is Goumang," it means proclaiming ordinances so people observe seasonal work—each month has its own decree. It does not mean the Son of Heaven performs a monthly new-moon sacrifice to paired emperors.

sentences.zh: 告朔者，諸侯禮也，《春秋》：『既視朔，遂登臺。』

translations.literal: Announcing the new moon was the rite of feudal lords; the "Spring and Autumn Annals" states: "Having inspected the new moon, he then ascended the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Announcing the new moon was a feudal-lord rite. The "Spring and Autumn Annals" records: "Having inspected the new moon, he then ascended the tower.

sentences.zh: 玄又說人君月告朔於廟，其祭為朝享。

translations.literal: Xuan also said that the ruler announces the new moon each month in the ancestral temple, and that the sacrifice is the morning audience.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also held that the ruler announces the new moon monthly in the ancestral temple and that the sacrifice constitutes the morning audience.

sentences.zh: 魯自文公始不視朔，明非天子所行。

translations.literal: From Duke Wen of Lu onward Lu ceased inspecting the new moon—clear proof that this was not what the Son of Heaven performed.
translations.idiomatic: From Duke Wen of Lu onward Lu stopped inspecting the new moon—clear evidence that this was not a Son-of-Heaven rite.

sentences.zh: 玄謂告帝即人帝，神即重、黎、五官，不言天子拜祭。

translations.literal: Xuan said that "emperor" means the human emperor and "spirit" means Chong, Li, and the Five Officials, and did not say the Son of Heaven bowed in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan took "emperor" to mean the human emperor and "spirit" to mean Chong, Li, and the Five Officials, yet never said the Son of Heaven bowed in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 臣請罷告朔、月祭，以應古禮。」

translations.literal: Your servant requests that announcing the new moon and the monthly sacrifice be abolished, in accord with ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask that the monthly announcement and monthly sacrifice be abolished, in keeping with ancient ritual.

sentences.zh: 齊賢不韙其說，質曰：「穀梁氏稱『閏月，天子不告朔』，它月故告朔矣。

translations.literal: Qixian did not approve of this view and rebutted, saying: "The Guliang tradition states, 'In an intercalary month the Son of Heaven does not announce the new moon'—which shows that in other months he did announce it.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian rejected this view and replied: "The Guliang tradition says, 'In an intercalary month the Son of Heaven does not announce the new moon'—which implies that in ordinary months he did.

sentences.zh: 左氏言魯『不告閏朔，為棄時政』，則諸侯雖閏告朔矣。

translations.literal: The Zuo tradition says that Lu 'did not announce the intercalary new moon, thereby abandoning timely government'—which shows that even feudal lords announced the new moon in intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo commentary says Lu "failed to announce the intercalary new moon, thereby abandoning timely government"—showing that feudal lords too announced the new moon in intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 《周太史》『頒朔於邦國』，《玉藻》『閏月，王居門』，是天子雖閏亦告朔。

translations.literal: The "Zhou Grand Astrologer" says "Distribute the new moon to the states," and the "Jade Regalia" says "In an intercalary month the king dwells at the gate"—showing that even in intercalary months the Son of Heaven announces the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The "Zhou Grand Astrologer" says "Distribute the new moon to the states," and the "Jade Regalia" says "In an intercalary month the king dwells at the gate"—showing that the Son of Heaven announced the new moon even in intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 二家去聖不遠，載天子、諸侯告朔事，顯顯弗繆。

translations.literal: These two schools were not far removed from the sages, and they record the Son of Heaven and feudal lords announcing the new moon—plainly without error.
translations.idiomatic: These two traditions lie close to the sages themselves, and their records of Son-of-Heaven and feudal-lord new-moon rites are plainly sound.

sentences.zh: 今議者乃以《太宰》正月之吉，布治邦國，而言天子元日一告朔，殊失其旨。

translations.literal: Those debating now take the "Grand Steward" passage on the auspicious day of the first month promulgating government throughout the states and say the Son of Heaven announces the new moon only once on New Year's Day—a grave misreading of the text.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters now cite the "Grand Steward" passage about promulgating government on the first month's auspicious day and conclude that the Son of Heaven announced the new moon only once a year on New Year's Day—a serious misreading.

sentences.zh: 一歲之元，六官自布所職之典。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the year, the six officials each promulgate the statutes of their own offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the year's opening, each of the six officials promulgates the ordinances of his own department.

sentences.zh: 幹寶謂吉為朔，故世人繆吉為告，據繆失經，不得為法。

translations.literal: Gan Bao took "auspicious" to mean the new moon, so later men mistakenly took "auspicious" to mean "announce"; relying on error against the classics, this cannot serve as law.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao equated "auspicious day" with "new-moon day," and later scholars wrongly equated "auspicious" with "announce." To build law on such a mistake is to abandon the classics.

sentences.zh: 議者又引左氏說，專在諸侯，不知《玉藻》與左說正同，而獨於天子言歲首一告，何去取之恣也！

translations.literal: The debaters also cite the Zuo tradition, applying it solely to feudal lords, unaware that the "Jade Regalia" agrees with the Zuo account—yet they single out for the Son of Heaven only one announcement at the year's start. How arbitrary to take and discard as they please!
translations.idiomatic: They also cite the Zuo tradition as if it applied only to feudal lords, not seeing that the "Jade Regalia" agrees with Zuo—yet they grant the Son of Heaven only a single year-opening announcement. What arbitrary picking and choosing!

sentences.zh: 又謂時帝，五人帝也。

translations.literal: They also say the seasonal emperor means the Five Human Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: They further hold that the seasonal emperor refers to the Five Human Emperors.

sentences.zh: 玄於時帝包天人，故以文、武作配，是並告兩五帝為不疑。

translations.literal: Xuan's seasonal emperor embraced Heaven and man, hence he paired King Wen and King Wu—thereby announcing to both sets of Five Emperors without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: For Zheng Xuan the seasonal emperor united Heaven and man, which is why he paired King Wen and King Wu—thereby announcing to both pentads of emperors without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 諸侯受朔天子，藏於廟。

translations.literal: Feudal lords received the new moon from the Son of Heaven and stored it in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords received the calendar from the Son of Heaven and kept it in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 天子受朔於天，宜在明堂，故告時帝，配祖考。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven received the new moon from Heaven and should do so at the Bright Hall; hence he announces to the seasonal emperor and associates his forefathers.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven received the new moon from Heaven and properly did so at the Bright Hall, announcing to the seasonal emperor with his ancestors as associates.

sentences.zh: 議者曰：『天子月告祭頒朔，則諸侯安得藏之？

translations.literal: The debaters say: "If the Son of Heaven announces sacrifice and distributes the new moon every month, how could feudal lords store it?
translations.idiomatic: The debaters object: "If the Son of Heaven performed monthly sacrificial announcements and distributed the new moon, how could feudal lords keep it in storage?

sentences.zh: 故太宰歲首布一歲事，太史頒之也。』

translations.literal: Therefore the Grand Steward at the year's start promulgates the year's business once, and the Grand Astrologer distributes it.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Grand Steward promulgates the year's business once at the year's opening, and the Grand Astrologer distributes it.

sentences.zh: 是不然。

translations.literal: That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: That is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 《周太史》『頒朔邦國』，是總頒十二朔於諸侯；

translations.literal: The "Zhou Grand Astrologer" says "Distribute the new moon to the states"—meaning to distribute all twelve new moons to the feudal lords in total;
translations.idiomatic: The "Zhou Grand Astrologer" says "Distribute the new moon to the states"—meaning to issue all twelve monthly new moons to the feudal lords at once;

sentences.zh: 天子猶月告者，頒官府都鄙也。

translations.literal: that the Son of Heaven still announces monthly is to distribute them to the government offices and districts.
translations.idiomatic: while the Son of Heaven's continuing monthly announcement distributes them to government offices and districts.

sentences.zh: 內外異言之也。

translations.literal: The inner and outer realms speak differently of this.
translations.idiomatic: This is a difference between what is said of the inner court and what is said of the outer realm.

sentences.zh: 禮不可罷。」

translations.literal: The rite cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The rite must not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎王方慶又推言：「明堂，布政之宮，所以明天氣，統萬物也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Wang Fangqing further argued: "The Bright Hall is the palace for promulgating government, by which one clarifies Heaven's qi and governs the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Fangqing of the Phoenix Pavilion added: "The Bright Hall is the hall of government, where Heaven's influence is made manifest and the myriad things are brought into order.

sentences.zh: 漢儒以明堂、太廟為一，宗祀其祖，而配上帝。

translations.literal: Han scholars took the Bright Hall and the Grand Ancestral Temple as one; they honored their ancestors in sacrifice and paired them with the Supreme Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Han scholars identified the Bright Hall with the Grand Ancestral Temple, honoring ancestors in sacrifice and pairing them with the Supreme Emperor.

sentences.zh: 取宗祀曰清廟，正室為太室，向陽為明堂，建學為太學，圜水為辟雍，異名同事，古之制也。

translations.literal: Calling the ancestral shrine the Pure Temple, the central chamber the Grand Chamber, the south-facing hall the Bright Hall, the established school the Grand Academy, and the encircled water the Enclosing Moat—these are different names for the same institution, an ancient arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral shrine was called the Pure Temple, the central chamber the Grand Chamber, the south-facing hall the Bright Hall, the imperial academy the Grand Academy, and the encircled pond the Enclosing Moat—different names for one institution, as antiquity arranged it.

sentences.zh: 天子以正月上辛總受十二月政於南郊，還藏於祖廟，月取一政，班之明堂。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven on the first xin day of the first month altogether received the twelve months' government at the southern suburb, then returned and stored it in the ancestral temple; each month he took one ordinance and promulgated it in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xin day of the first month the Son of Heaven received the full year's ordinances at the southern suburb, stored them in the ancestral temple, and each month took one ordinance to promulgate in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 諸侯則受於天子，藏之祖廟，月取一政，行之於國。

translations.literal: Feudal lords then received it from the Son of Heaven, stored it in the ancestral temple, took one ordinance each month, and carried it out in their states.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords received the calendar from the Son of Heaven, kept it in the ancestral temple, and enacted one ordinance per month within their domains.

sentences.zh: 王者以其禮告廟，謂之告朔；

translations.literal: When the king reported this rite to the temple, it was called announcing the new moon;
translations.idiomatic: When the king reported this rite to the temple, it was called announcing the new moon;

sentences.zh: 視月之政，謂之視朔。

translations.literal: when he inspected the month's government, it was called inspecting the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: when he reviewed the month's ordinances, it was called inspecting the new moon.

sentences.zh: 《玉藻》：『玄冕而朝日東門之外，聽朔南門之外。』

translations.literal: The "Jade Regalia" states: "Wearing the dark cap, he faces the sun outside the eastern gate; he receives the new moon outside the southern gate."
translations.idiomatic: The "Jade Regalia" reads: "Wearing the dark ceremonial cap, he faces the sun outside the eastern gate and receives the new moon outside the southern gate."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄說：『明堂在國陽，就其時之堂而聽朔焉。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan explained: "The Bright Hall stands in the yang of the capital; one goes to the hall of the season and receives the new moon there.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explained: "The Bright Hall stands in the capital's sunny quarter; one goes to the seasonal hall to receive the new moon.

sentences.zh: 卒事，宿路寢。』

translations.literal: When the rite is finished, one lodges in the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite is complete, one lodges in the inner chamber.

sentences.zh: 今元日通天宮受朝，有司遂讀時令、布政，古之禮也。

translations.literal: Now, receiving court on New Year's Day at the Tongtian Palace, where the relevant offices then read the seasonal ordinances and promulgate government, is the ancient rite.
translations.idiomatic: Today's New Year audience at the Tongtian Palace, followed by the reading of seasonal ordinances and promulgation of government, follows the ancient rite.

sentences.zh: 舊說天子歲入明堂者十八：大享，一；

translations.literal: Older accounts say the Son of Heaven entered the Bright Hall eighteen times in a year: the great offering, one;
translations.idiomatic: Older accounts say the Son of Heaven entered the Bright Hall eighteen times a year: the great offering, once;

sentences.zh: 月告朔，十二；

translations.literal: monthly announcement of the new moon, twelve;
translations.idiomatic: monthly new-moon announcements, twelve;

sentences.zh: 四時迎氣，四；

translations.literal: welcoming the qi of the four seasons, four;
translations.idiomatic: welcoming the qi of the four seasons, four;

sentences.zh: 巡狩之歲，一。

translations.literal: in years of the imperial tour of inspection, one.
translations.idiomatic: and in years of the imperial tour, once.

sentences.zh: 今議者唯許歲首一入，不亦隘乎？

translations.literal: Those debating now permit entry only at the year's start—is that not too narrow?
translations.idiomatic: The debaters now allow only a single annual entry—is that not unduly restrictive?

sentences.zh: 陛下幸建明堂，遵用告朔事，若月一聽，則近於煩，每孟月視朔，惟制定其禮，臣下不敢專。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has graciously built the Bright Hall and wishes to follow the rite of announcing the new moon; if one were to receive it every month, that would approach excessive frequency. Let Your Majesty inspect the new moon each first month of the season and fix the rite by imperial decision—the ministers dare not decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has built the Bright Hall and wishes to restore the new-moon announcement. A monthly audience would verge on excessive; let Your Majesty inspect the new moon at the start of each season and settle the rite by edict—we ministers dare not decide on our own.

sentences.zh: 成均博士吳楊吾等共言：「秦滅學，告朔禮廢。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Directorate of Education Wu Yangwu and others jointly said: "When the Qin extinguished learning, the rite of announcing the new moon was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Wu Yangwu and others of the Directorate of Education jointly argued: "When the Qin suppressed learning, the new-moon rite fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 今用四孟月、季夏，至明堂告五時帝堂上，請兼如齊賢、方慶議。」

translations.literal: Now, using the four first months of the seasons and the last month of summer, go to the Bright Hall to announce to the Five Seasonal Emperors in the upper hall—please adopt both Qixian's and Fangqing's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: We propose using the four seasonal first months and the last month of summer to announce to the Five Seasonal Emperors in the Bright Hall's upper chamber—combining the recommendations of Qixian and Fangqing.

sentences.zh: 不數歲，禮亦廢。

translations.literal: Within a few years the rite was again abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the rite lapsed once more.

sentences.zh: 久之，齊賢遷博士。

translations.literal: After some time Qixian was transferred to erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qixian was promoted to erudite.

sentences.zh: 時東都置太社，禮部尚書祝欽明問禮官博士：「周家田主用所宜木，今社主石，奈何？」

translations.literal: At that time the Eastern Capital established the Grand Earth Altar; Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming questioned the ritual officials and erudites: "The Zhou used the appropriate tree for the field lord; today the altar lord is stone—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital established the Grand Earth Altar, Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming asked the ritual officials and erudites: "The Zhou used the appropriate tree for the field lord, but our altar lord is stone—what should we do?"

sentences.zh: 齊賢與太常少卿韋叔夏、國子司業郭山惲、尹知章等議：「《春秋》：『君以軍行，祓社釁鼓，祝奉以從。』

translations.literal: Qixian, together with Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Shuxia, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education Guo Shanyun, Yin Zhizhang, and others, deliberated: "The "Spring and Autumn Annals" states: "When the ruler goes forth with the army, he purifies the altar of the soil and smears blood on the drums; the invocator carries it and follows.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian, Vice Director Wei Shuxia of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Vice Director Guo Shanyun of the Directorate of Education, Yin Zhizhang, and others replied: "The "Spring and Autumn Annals" records: "When the ruler marches with the army, he purifies the soil altar and smears blood on the drums; the invocator carries the lord and follows.

sentences.zh: 故曰：『不用命，戮於社。』

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "Those who do not obey orders are executed at the altar of the soil.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Those who disobey orders are executed before the soil altar.

sentences.zh: 社稷主用石，以可奉而行也。

translations.literal: Therefore the lords of the altars of soil and grain use stone, because stone can be carried and moved.
translations.idiomatic: The lords of the altars of soil and grain are therefore made of stone, because stone can be carried on campaign.

sentences.zh: 崔靈恩曰：『社主用石，以地產最實歟！』

translations.literal: Cui Lingen said: "The altar lord uses stone because earth's product is most solid!"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lingen said: "The altar lord is stone because earth's product is the most solid!"

sentences.zh: 《呂氏春秋》言『殷人社用石』。

translations.literal: The "Mr. Lü's Spring and Autumn Annals" says "The altar of the Yin people used stone."
translations.idiomatic: The "Mr. Lü's Spring and Autumn Annals" states that "the Yin people's altar used stone."

sentences.zh: 後魏天平中，遷太社石主，其來尚矣。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era of Later Wei the stone lord of the Grand Altar was moved—its origin is indeed ancient.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era of Later Wei the stone lord of the Grand Altar was moved—so the practice is very old.

sentences.zh: 周之田主用所宜木，其民間之社歟！

translations.literal: The Zhou field lord used the appropriate tree—was that the altar of the common people!
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou used the appropriate tree for the field lord, that referred to the common people's altars!

sentences.zh: 非太社也。」

translations.literal: It was not the Grand Altar."
translations.idiomatic: It was not the Grand Altar."

sentences.zh: 於是舊主長尺有六寸，方尺七寸，問博士雲何，齊賢等議：「社主之制，禮無傳。

translations.literal: Thereupon the old lord was one foot and six inches long and one foot seven inches square; when the erudites were asked what should be done, Qixian and others deliberated: "The regulations for the altar lord have no transmitted standard.
translations.idiomatic: The existing lord measured one foot six inches long and one foot seven inches square. When the erudites were consulted, Qixian and his colleagues argued: "The dimensions of the altar lord are nowhere prescribed in the rites.

sentences.zh: 天子親征，載以行，則非過重。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven personally campaigns, it is carried on the march—so it cannot be excessively heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven campaigns in person, the lord travels with the army—it cannot be too heavy.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：『社祭土，主陰氣。』

translations.literal: The "Rites" state: "In sacrificing to the altar of soil one sacrifices to earth; the lord represents yin qi.
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites" say: "In sacrificing to the soil altar one sacrifices to earth; the lord represents yin qi.

sentences.zh: 《韓詩外傳》：『天子太社方五丈，諸侯半之。』

translations.literal: The "Han Poetry Outer Commentary" states: "The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Soil is five zhang square; feudal lords have half that.
translations.idiomatic: The "Han Poetry Outer Commentary" says: "The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Soil is five zhang square; feudal lords use half that size.

sentences.zh: 五，土數。

translations.literal: Five is the number of earth.
translations.idiomatic: Five is earth's number.

sentences.zh: 社主宜長五尺，以準數五；

translations.literal: The altar lord should be five chi long, to match the number five;
translations.idiomatic: The altar lord should therefore be five chi long, matching the number five;

sentences.zh: 方二尺，以準陰偶；

translations.literal: two chi square, to match yin's evenness;
translations.idiomatic: two chi square, matching yin's even quality;

sentences.zh: 剡其上，以象物生；

translations.literal: tapered at the top, to represent things being born;
translations.idiomatic: tapered above, representing things coming into being;

sentences.zh: 方其下，以象地體；

translations.literal: squared at the bottom, to represent the body of earth;
translations.idiomatic: squared below, representing the form of earth;

sentences.zh: 埋半土中，本末均也。

translations.literal: half buried in the soil, root and crown equal.
translations.idiomatic: half buried in soil, root and crown equal.

sentences.zh: 請度以古尺」雲。

translations.literal: Please measure by the ancient foot."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that it be measured by the ancient foot."

sentences.zh: 又問：「社稷壇隨四方用色，而中不數尺，冒黃土，謂何？」

translations.literal: They were asked again: "The altars of soil and grain follow the four directions in color, yet at the center, not several chi across, yellow earth covers them—what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: They were asked further: "The altars of soil and grain are colored by the four directions, yet at the center, over only a few chi, yellow earth is piled—what is the meaning of this?"

sentences.zh: 齊賢等曰：「天子太社，度廣五丈，分四方，上冒黃土，象王者覆被四方，然則當以黃土覆壇上。

translations.literal: Qixian and others said: "The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Soil is five zhang wide; divided into four quarters, with yellow earth heaped on top—it represents the king covering the four quarters. Therefore yellow earth should cover the top of the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian and his colleagues replied: "The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Soil is five zhang wide, divided into four quarters, with yellow earth heaped on top—symbolizing the king's embrace of the four quarters. Yellow earth should therefore cover the entire altar top.

sentences.zh: 舊壇上不數尺，覆被之狹，乖於古。」

translations.literal: The old altar top, not several chi across, was too narrow in its covering—at odds with antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The old altar top, only a few chi across, covered too small an area and departed from ancient practice."

sentences.zh: 於是以方色飾壇四面及陛，而黃土全覆上焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the four sides of the altar and its steps were decorated with the colors of the quarters, and yellow earth wholly covered the top.
translations.idiomatic: The four sides of the altar and its steps were then decorated with the colors of the quarters, and yellow earth covered the top entirely.

sentences.zh: 祭牲皆太牢。

translations.literal: The sacrificial victims were all grand offerings.
translations.idiomatic: All sacrificial victims were grand offerings.

sentences.zh: 其後改先農曰「帝社」，又立「帝稷」，皆齊賢等參定。

translations.literal: Later the Former Farmer was changed to "Emperor's Altar of Soil," and "Emperor's Altar of Grain" was also established—both were determined with Qixian and others participating.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Former Farmer rite was renamed the "Emperor's Altar of Soil," and an "Emperor's Altar of Grain" was also established—both arrangements were settled with Qixian and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，因武後東都廟改為唐廟，議滿七室，以涼武昭王為始祖。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, the Eastern Capital temple that Empress Wu had established was changed to the Tang temple; debate arose over filling seven chambers, making Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong acceded, the Eastern Capital temple Empress Wu had established was converted into the Tang ancestral temple. Officials debated filling all seven chambers by making Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 齊賢上議：「《禮》，天子七廟，尊始封君曰太祖，百代不遷，始祖無聞焉。

translations.literal: Qixian submitted a memorial arguing: "The "Rites" prescribe seven temples for the Son of Heaven; the lord of the first enfeoffment is called the Grand Ancestor and is never displaced for a hundred generations—nowhere is a separate founding ancestor mentioned.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian submitted a memorial arguing: "The "Rites" prescribe seven temples for the Son of Heaven. The lord of the first enfeoffment is called the Grand Ancestor and is never displaced for a hundred generations—the rites nowhere mention a separate founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 殷自玄王至湯，周後稷至武王，皆出太祖後，合食有序。

translations.literal: From the Mysterious King in Yin down to Tang, and from Houji in Zhou down to King Wu—all descended from the Grand Ancestor, and their joint offerings were arranged in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: In both Yin and Zhou, from the Mysterious King down to Tang and from Houji down to King Wu, every line issued from the Grand Ancestor, and the order of their joint sacrificial feasting was fixed and proper.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝始封唐，實為太祖，以世數近，故尚在昭穆。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing was first enfeoffed with Tang and was in fact the Grand Ancestor; because the number of generations was close, he therefore remained within the zhao-mu arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing had been the first to receive the fief of Tang and was in truth the dynasty's Grand Ancestor; because so few generations separated him from the reigning house, he still held a place in the zhao-mu sequence.

sentences.zh: 今乃上引武昭王為始祖，異乎殷、周之本卨、稷也。

translations.literal: Now, however, one takes Prince Zhao of Wu as the founding ancestor—this differs from Yin and Zhou, whose foundations were Qi and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: To elevate Prince Zhao of Wu as founding ancestor now would diverge from the Yin and Zhou precedent, in which the founding lines traced back to Qi and Ji respectively.

sentences.zh: 卨、稷興胙，景皇帝是也。

translations.literal: It was Qi and Ji who rose through the sacrificial enfeoffments—Emperor Jing is such a one.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Qi and Ji had risen to eminence through enfeoffment and sacrificial standing, so too was Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 昭王國不世傳，後嗣失守。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao's state was not transmitted generation after generation, and later descendants lost hold of it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao's kingdom was not handed down through successive generations, and his later descendants forfeited it.

sentences.zh: 景帝實始封唐，子孫是承。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing truly was the first to be enfeoffed with Tang, and his descendants are the ones who inherit.
translations.idiomatic: It was Emperor Jing who had first received the enfeoffment of Tang, and it was his descendants who carried on the line.

sentences.zh: 若近舍唐，遠引涼，不見其可。

translations.literal: If one discards Tang when it is near and cites Liang from afar, one does not see how this can be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: To set aside nearby Tang and invoke distant Liang finds no justification.

sentences.zh: 且魏不祖曹參，晉不祖司馬卬，宋不祖楚元王，齊、梁不祖蕭何，陳、隋不祖胡公、楊震，今謂昭王為祖，可乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, Wei did not take Cao Shen as ancestor, Jin did not take Sima Ang, Song did not take the Prince of Chu, Yuan, Qi and Liang did not take Xiao He, Chen and Sui did not take Duke Hu and Yang Zhen—can one now declare Prince Zhao as ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: Wei did not enshrine Cao Shen as a dynastic forebear, nor Jin Sima Ang, Song the Prince of Chu, Yuan, nor Qi and Liang Xiao He, nor Chen and Sui Duke Hu and Yang Zhen—under such precedents, can Prince Zhao really be proclaimed founding ancestor?

sentences.zh: 漢以周郊後稷，議欲郊堯，杜林以為周興自後稷，漢業特起，功不緣堯，卒不果郊。

translations.literal: Han, following Zhou in offering suburban sacrifices to Houji, debated offering suburban sacrifice to Yao. Du Lin held that Zhou's rise began from Houji, whereas Han's enterprise arose on its own—its merit did not derive from Yao—and in the end the suburban sacrifice to Yao was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Han, like the Zhou, sacrificed to Houji at the suburban altar; there was discussion of sacrificing to Yao as well, but Du Lin argued that while Zhou's rise proceeded from Houji, Han's empire had sprung up independently, its achievement owing nothing to Yao—and in the end no sacrifice to Yao was performed.

sentences.zh: 武德初定，去昭王尤近，不托祖者，不可故也。

translations.literal: When the Wude era was first established, one was especially close to Prince Zhao, yet did not invoke him as ancestor—this cannot be for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude reign, when Prince Zhao lay within living memory, the dynasty nonetheless refrained from making him its forebear—and that restraint cannot have been without cause.

sentences.zh: 今而立之，非祖宗意。

translations.literal: Now to establish him as such would not accord with the intentions of the ancestral spirits.
translations.idiomatic: To install him as ancestor now would go against what the forefathers intended.

sentences.zh: 景皇失位，神弗臨享，殆非詒厥孫謀者。」

translations.literal: Emperor Jing loses his seat; the spirits do not descend to receive offerings—this is scarcely what it means to 'bequeath plans to one's descendants.'
translations.idiomatic: To displace Emperor Jing would mean the spirits no longer receive his offerings—hardly the kind of legacy one bequeaths to posterity.

sentences.zh: 博士劉承慶、尹知章又言：「受命之君，王跡有淺深，代系有遠邇。

translations.literal: Erudite scholars Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also said: 'For a ruler who receives the Mandate, the traces of royal achievement vary in depth, and the dynastic lineage varies in distance.
translations.idiomatic: The Erudites Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also submitted: 'A ruler who receives the Mandate may leave traces of kingship that are shallow or deep, and the line of succession may stretch back near or far.

sentences.zh: 祖以功，昭穆以親。

translations.literal: Ancestry is by merit; zhao-mu placement is by kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Founding ancestry is determined by merit; placement in the zhao-mu system is determined by closeness of kin.

sentences.zh: 有功者不遷，親盡者毀。

translations.literal: Those with merit are not moved; when kinship is exhausted, the shrine is destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy forebears are never displaced; when closeness of kin runs out, their tablets are removed.

sentences.zh: 今不宜以廟數未備，引當遷之主於昭穆上，茍充七室也。

translations.literal: At present one should not, because the number of temple chambers is not yet complete, bring forth lords who ought to be moved and place them within zhao-mu merely to fill out seven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: One ought not, merely because the temple lacks a full complement of chambers, drag in ancestors due for removal and seat them in the zhao-mu sequence just to make up seven shrines.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝既號太祖，以世淺猶在六室位，則室未當有七，非天子廟不當七也。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Jing is already styled Grand Ancestor, and because the generations are shallow he still occupies a place among the six chambers, the chambers ought not to number seven—not that a Son of Heaven's temple should not have seven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing already bears the title of Grand Ancestor and, generations being so few, still holds one of the six shrines—therefore the temple should not yet have seven chambers; this is not a denial that an emperor's temple may eventually reach seven.

sentences.zh: 大帝神主既祔，宣皇帝當遷。

translations.literal: Once the spirit tablet of the Great Emperor has been enshrined alongside, Emperor Xuan ought to be moved out.
translations.idiomatic: After the Great Emperor's tablet has been installed in the shared rite, Emperor Xuan should be transferred from the main temple.

sentences.zh: 宣非始祖，又無宗號，親盡而遷，不可復立。

translations.literal: Xuan was not the founding ancestor, nor does he have a honorific temple title; when kinship is exhausted he is moved, and cannot be re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was neither founding ancestor nor holder of a temple honorific; once the bond of kinship expired he was due for removal, and there is no grounds to restore his shrine.

sentences.zh: 請仍為六室。」

translations.literal: We request that it remain six chambers.'
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the temple remain at six shrines.'

sentences.zh: 詔宰相詳裁。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chief ministers to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the chief ministers to examine the matter fully and decide.

sentences.zh: 於是祝欽明等上言：「博士等三百人為兩說：齊賢等不祖武昭王，劉承慶等請遷宣皇帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Qinming and others submitted: 'Among more than three hundred Erudites there are two positions: Qi Xian and others oppose taking Prince Zhao of Wu as ancestor; Liu Chengqing and others request that Emperor Xuan be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qinming and his colleagues then memorialized: 'Of the three hundred-odd Erudites, two schools have emerged—Qi Xian's party opposes honoring Prince Zhao of Wu as ancestor, while Liu Chengqing's party asks that Emperor Xuan be removed from the temple.

sentences.zh: 臣等欲皆可其奏。」

translations.literal: Your subjects wish to approve both memorials.
translations.idiomatic: We propose to approve both positions.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict granted approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented by edict.

sentences.zh: 俄以孝敬皇帝為義宗，列於廟為七室。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, the filial and reverent emperor was made Honorific Ancestor, listed in the temple as seven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Xiaojing was installed as the Honorific Ancestor, bringing the temple to seven shrines.

sentences.zh: 西京太廟亦如之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestral Temple in the Western Capital was likewise arranged.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple in the western capital was organized in the same way.

sentences.zh: 齊賢遷累諫議大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Qi Xian was transferred and promoted repeatedly to Remonstrating Advisor, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xian rose through successive postings to Remonstrating Advisor and then died.

sentences.zh: 柳沖，蒲州虞鄉人，隋饒州刺史莊曾孫。

translations.literal: Liu Chong was a native of Yuxiang in Pu Prefecture, the great-grandson of Zhuang, prefect of Raozhou under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong came from Yuxiang in Pu Prefecture; he was the great-grandson of Zhuang, who had served as prefect of Raozhou under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 父楚賢，大業中為河北縣長。

translations.literal: His father Chu Xian served as magistrate of Hebei County during the Daye era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chu Xian was magistrate of Hebei County in the Daye reign.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵興，堯君素據郡固守，楚賢說曰：「隋之亡，天下共知。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised his army, Yao Junsu held the commandery and defended it stubbornly. Chu Xian urged him, saying: 'The fall of Sui is known to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took up arms, Yao Junsu held the commandery and refused to yield. Chu Xian remonstrated with him: 'Everyone knows the Sui dynasty is finished.

sentences.zh: 唐公名在圖箓，動以誠信，豪英景赴，天所贊也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang's name is in the apocryphal charts and texts; he acts with sincerity and trustworthiness, and heroes and worthies flock to him at the sight of his brilliance—this is what Heaven approves.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang's name appears in the prophetic registers; he moves with sincerity and good faith, and heroes flock to his radiance—that is Heaven's chosen man.

sentences.zh: 君子見幾而作，俟終日邪？」

translations.literal: The superior man acts when he sees the first sign—must he wait until the end of the day?
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman acts at the first hint of change—why wait until the day is spent?

sentences.zh: 君素不從，楚賢潛行自歸，授侍御史。

translations.literal: Junsu would not follow his advice; Chu Xian went secretly and came over on his own, and was appointed Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu refused to listen. Chu Xian slipped away to join the Tang camp and was appointed Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，持節冊拜突厥，辭其遺不受。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, bearing credentials he went to invest the Turks with title, but declined their gifts and did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan reign he was dispatched with imperial credentials to invest the Turks but declined the gifts they offered.

sentences.zh: 歷交、桂二州都督、杭州刺史，皆有名。

translations.literal: He served successively as military governor of Jiao and Gui Prefectures and as prefect of Hang Prefecture—all with distinguished reputations.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts as military governor of Jiao and Gui and as prefect of Hangzhou, earning renown at each.

sentences.zh: 沖好學，多所研總。

translations.literal: Liu Chong loved learning and pursued broad investigation and synthesis.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong was devoted to scholarship and pursued wide-ranging study with thorough mastery.

sentences.zh: 天授初，為司府寺主簿，詔遣安撫淮南，使有指，封河東縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianshou era he served as chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Household. He was ordered on a mission to pacify Huainan; his commission achieved its aim, and he was enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshou reign he served as chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Household, then was dispatched to pacify Huainan. His mission succeeded, and he was created Baron of Hedong County.

sentences.zh: 中宗景龍中，遷左散騎常侍，修國史。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era of Emperor Zhongzong he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant and worked on the national history.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Zhongzong's Jinglong reign he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Left and joined in compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗命諸儒撰《氏族志》，甄差群姓。

translations.literal: At first, Emperor Taizong ordered the various scholars to compile the Register of Clans, sorting and ranking the many surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had ordered scholars to compile the Register of Clans, classifying the great surname groups.

sentences.zh: 其後門胄興替不常，沖請改修其書，帝詔魏元忠、張錫、蕭至忠、岑羲、崔湜、徐堅、劉憲、吳兢及沖共取德、功、時望、國籍之家，等而次之。

translations.literal: Thereafter, as noble clans rose and fell without constancy, Liu Chong requested a revised edition of the work. The emperor ordered Wei Yuanzhong, Zhang Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, Cui Shi, Xu Jian, Liu Xian, Wu Jing, and Liu Chong jointly to select families distinguished by virtue, merit, contemporary standing, and registered lineage, and to rank them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as noble houses waxed and waned unpredictably, Liu Chong petitioned for a revision. The emperor charged Wei Yuanzhong, Zhang Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, Cui Shi, Xu Jian, Liu Xian, Wu Jing, and Liu Chong to rank families by virtue, achievement, contemporary eminence, and official registration.

sentences.zh: 夷蕃酋長襲冠帶者，析著別品。

translations.literal: For tribal chieftains of foreign peoples who had received caps and sashes by inheritance, separate categories were set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders from border peoples who had inherited Chinese titles and dress were assigned separate categories.

sentences.zh: 會元忠等繼物故，至先天時，復詔沖及堅、兢與魏知古、陸象先、劉子玄等討綴，書乃成，號《姓系錄》。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhong and the others died in succession, by the Xiantian era the emperor again ordered Liu Chong, together with Xu Jian, Wu Jing, Wei Zhigu, Lu Xiangxian, and Liu Zixuan, to discuss and complete it; the work was finished and titled Genealogical Record of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanzhong and several others died in turn, in the Xiantian reign Liu Chong was again ordered to work with Xu Jian, Wu Jing, Wei Zhigu, Lu Xiangxian, and Liu Zixuan to finish the compilation. The completed work was titled the Genealogical Record of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 歷太子賓客、宋王師、昭文館學士，以老致仕。

translations.literal: He served successively as Guest of the Heir Apparent, tutor to the Prince of Song, and academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Guest of the Heir Apparent, tutor to the Prince of Song, and academician of the Zhaowen Hall before retiring in old age.

sentences.zh: 開元初，詔沖與薛南金復加刊竄，乃定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, Liu Chong and Xue Nanjin were ordered to edit and revise the work again, after which it was finalized.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Liu Chong and Xue Nanjin were charged with another round of editing before the work was finally settled.

sentences.zh: 後柳芳著論甚詳，今刪其要，著之左方。

translations.literal: Later Liu Fang wrote a treatise in great detail; now its essentials are excerpted and recorded in the left column.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang later wrote a detailed treatise on the subject; what follows is an abridgment of its main points.

sentences.zh: 芳之言曰：

translations.literal: Liu Fang's words say:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang wrote:

sentences.zh: 氏族者，古史官所記也。

translations.literal: Clans and surnames are what the ancient historiographers recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The records of clans and surnames were kept by the historiographers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 昔周小史定系世，辯昭穆，故古有《世本》，錄黃帝以來至春秋時諸侯、卿、大夫名號繼統。

translations.literal: Formerly the minor scribe of Zhou fixed genealogies and distinguished zhao from mu; hence in antiquity there was the Genealogical Annals, recording from the Yellow Emperor down to the Spring and Autumn period the titles and lines of succession of feudal lords, ministers, and grandees.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou times minor scribes fixed genealogies and sorted zhao from mu; hence the ancient Genealogical Annals, which recorded the titles and succession lines of lords, ministers, and grandees from the Yellow Emperor down to the Spring and Autumn era.

sentences.zh: 左丘明傳《春秋》，亦言：「天子建德，因生以賜姓，胙之土，命之氏；

translations.literal: Zuo Qiuming, in transmitting the Spring and Autumn Annals, also said: 'The Son of Heaven bestows virtue; in accordance with birth he grants the surname, enfeoffs with sacrificial land, and assigns the clan name;
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Qiuming, commentator on the Spring and Autumn Annals, likewise wrote: 'The Son of Heaven establishes virtue; based on the circumstances of birth he bestows a surname, grants sacrificial land as enfeoffment, and assigns a clan name;

sentences.zh: 諸侯以字為氏，以謚為族。」

translations.literal: Feudal lords take the courtesy name as clan name and the posthumous title as lineage branch.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords take their courtesy names as clan names and their posthumous titles as lineage designations.

sentences.zh: 昔堯賜伯禹姓曰姒，氏曰有夏；

translations.literal: Formerly Yao granted Bo Yu the surname Si and the clan name Youxia;
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times Yao gave Bo Yu the surname Si and the clan designation Youxia;

sentences.zh: 伯夷姓曰姜，氏曰有呂。

translations.literal: Bo Yi had the surname Jiang and the clan name Youlyu.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi bore the surname Jiang and the clan name Youlyu.

sentences.zh: 下及三代，官有世功，則有官族，邑亦如之。

translations.literal: Down through the Three Dynasties, when an office passed down through generations for accumulated merit, there was an official clan name; enfeoffments followed the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Three Dynasties, offices held across generations for accumulated merit gave rise to official clan names; enfeoffments worked the same way.

sentences.zh: 後世或氏於國，則齊、魯、秦、吳；

translations.literal: In later ages some took clan names from states—such as Qi, Lu, Qin, and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: In later ages some derived clan names from states—Qi, Lu, Qin, Wu;

sentences.zh: 氏於謚，則文、武、成、宣；

translations.literal: from posthumous titles—such as Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: from posthumous titles—Wen, Wu, Cheng, Xuan;

sentences.zh: 氏於官，則司馬、司徒；

translations.literal: from offices—such as Sima and Situ;
translations.idiomatic: from offices—Sima, Situ;

sentences.zh: 氏於爵，則王孫、公孫；

translations.literal: from ranks—such as Wangsun and Gongsun;
translations.idiomatic: from noble ranks—Wangsun, Gongsun;

sentences.zh: 氏於字，則孟孫、叔孫；

translations.literal: from courtesy names—such as Mengsun and Shusun;
translations.idiomatic: from courtesy names—Mengsun, Shusun;

sentences.zh: 氏於居，則東門、北郭；

translations.literal: from residence—such as Dongmen and Beiguo;
translations.idiomatic: from places of residence—Dongmen, Beiguo;

sentences.zh: 氏於誌，則三烏、五鹿；

translations.literal: from memorial intent—such as Sanwu and Wulu;
translations.idiomatic: from personal aspiration—Sanwu, Wulu;

sentences.zh: 氏於事，則巫、乙、匠、陶。

translations.literal: from occupations—such as Wu, Yi, Jiang, and Tao.
translations.idiomatic: from occupation—Wu, Yi, Jiang, Tao.

sentences.zh: 於是受姓命氏，粲然眾矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon, receiving surnames and receiving clan names, they became splendidly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: And so, with surnames and clan names granted in every manner, they proliferated in dazzling variety.

sentences.zh: 秦既滅學，公侯子孫失其本系。

translations.literal: After Qin extinguished learning, the descendants of dukes and marquises lost their original genealogies.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin suppressed scholarship, the descendants of the feudal nobility lost track of their ancestral lines.

sentences.zh: 漢興，司馬遷父子乃約《世本》修《史記》，因周譜明世家，乃知姓氏之所由出，虞、夏、商、周、昆吾、大彭、豕韋、齊桓、晉文皆同祖也。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Sima Qian and his father condensed the Genealogical Annals to compile the Records of the Grand Historian; relying on Zhou genealogies they clarified the hereditary houses, and thus came to know the origins of surnames—that Yu, Xia, Shang, Zhou, Kunwu, Dapeng, Shiwei, Duke Huan of Qi, and Duke Wen of Jin all shared common ancestry.
translations.idiomatic: At the rise of Han, Sima Qian and his father drew on the Genealogical Annals to compile the Records of the Grand Historian; using Zhou genealogical tables they clarified the great lineages and traced surnames to their origins, revealing that the lines of Yu, Xia, Shang, Zhou, Kunwu, Dapeng, Shiwei, Duke Huan of Qi, and Duke Wen of Jin all shared a common ancestry.

sentences.zh: 更王叠霸，多者千祀，少者數十代。

translations.literal: Kings replaced one another and hegemony overlapped; the longest lasted a thousand years of sacrifice, the shortest only several dozen generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thrones changed hands and hegemony passed in succession; some lines endured a thousand years of rites, others only a few dozen generations.

sentences.zh: 先王之封既絕，後嗣蒙其福，猶為強家。

translations.literal: Though the enfeoffments of the former kings had ended, later descendants who enjoyed their blessings still remained powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the feudal grants of the ancient kings lapsed, descendants who still basked in their legacy remained powerful clans.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝興徒步，有天下，命官以賢，詔爵以功，誓曰：「非劉氏王、無功侯者，天下共誅之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaodi of Han rose from common walking to possess the realm; he appointed officials for merit and enfeoffed for achievement, swearing: 'Whoever is not of the Liu clan made king, or made marquis without achievement—let the realm together execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaodi of Han rose from the ranks to win the realm; he appointed officials by talent and enfeoffed by merit, swearing: 'Any non-Liu made king or any marquis created without merit shall be put to death by all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 先王公卿之胄，才則用，不才棄之，不辨士與庶族，然則始尚官矣。

translations.literal: The descendants of former kings, dukes, and ministers—if talented they were employed; if untalented they were cast aside. No distinction was made between gentry and common clans—thus office was first honored.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the old royal and ministerial houses were employed if capable and dismissed if not, with no regard for gentry versus common stock—thus the Han era first honored official rank.

sentences.zh: 然猶徙山東豪傑以實京師，齊諸田，楚屈、景，皆右姓也。

translations.literal: Yet he still relocated the powerful families of east of the mountains to fill the capital; the many Tians of Qi and the Qu and Jing of Chu were all prominent surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still resettled powerful eastern families to fill the capital; the Tians of Qi and the Qu and Jing clans of Chu were all eminent surnames.

sentences.zh: 其後進拔豪英，論而錄之，蓋七相、五公之所由興也。

translations.literal: Thereafter, promoting and selecting heroic talents, recording them by evaluation—this was roughly how the seven chancellors and five high ministers came to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations promoted eminent men, assessed and recorded them in rank—and from this arose the tradition of the seven chancellors and five high ministers.

sentences.zh: 魏氏立九品，置中正，尊世胄，卑寒士，權歸右姓已。

translations.literal: The Wei dynasty established the nine-rank system, set up Rectifiers of Conduct, honored hereditary nobles, and held humble scholars in low regard—power already belonged to the prominent surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Wei instituted the nine-rank system and the Rectifier offices, elevating hereditary nobles and disdaining poor scholars—power had already passed to the great surname families.

sentences.zh: 其州大中正、主簿，郡中正、功曹，皆取著姓士族為之，以定門胄，品藻人物。

translations.literal: Their grand rectifiers and chief clerks at the prefectural level, and rectifiers and merit clerks at the commandery level, were all drawn from established-surname gentry clans, to fix the gates of noble lineage and evaluate men.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural grand rectifiers and chief clerks, along with commandery rectifiers and merit clerks, were all chosen from established gentry clans to fix lineage gates and rate men's qualifications.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋因之，始尚姓已。

translations.literal: Jin and Song followed this practice—surname prestige had already begun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Song adopted the same system—surname prestige was now firmly established.

sentences.zh: 然其別貴賤，分士庶，不可易也。

translations.literal: Yet the distinction between noble and base, gentry and commoners, could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the division between noble and low-born, gentry and commoner, had become unalterable.

sentences.zh: 於時有司選舉，必稽譜籍，而考其真偽。
