translations.literal: At that time, in official selection and recommendation, one had invariably to consult genealogical registers and verify their authenticity.
translations.idiomatic: In official recruitment, authorities invariably consulted genealogical registers and verified their authenticity.

sentences.zh: 故官有世胄，譜有世官，賈氏、王氏譜學出焉。

translations.literal: Thus offices had hereditary noble lines, registers had hereditary officials—and the genealogical scholarship of the Jia and Wang clans emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Offices passed through noble lines, registers tracked hereditary posts—and the genealogical expertise of the Jia and Wang families arose in response.

sentences.zh: 由是有譜局，令史職皆具。

translations.literal: Hence there were genealogical bureaus, with all the clerk positions fully staffed.
translations.idiomatic: Genealogical bureaus were established with a full complement of clerical staff.

sentences.zh: 過江則為「僑姓」，王、謝、袁、蕭為大；

translations.literal: After crossing the river they became 'émigré surnames'—Wang, Xie, Yuan, and Xiao were foremost;
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi came the 'émigré surnames,' led by the Wang, Xie, Yuan, and Xiao clans;

sentences.zh: 東南則為「吳姓」，朱、張、顧、陸為大；

translations.literal: in the southeast they became 'Wu surnames'—Zhu, Zhang, Gu, and Lu were foremost;
translations.idiomatic: in the southeast came the 'Wu surnames,' headed by Zhu, Zhang, Gu, and Lu;

sentences.zh: 山東則為「郡姓」，王、崔、盧、李、鄭為大；

translations.literal: in Shandong they became 'commandery surnames'—Wang, Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng were foremost;
translations.idiomatic: in Shandong came the 'commandery surnames,' dominated by Wang, Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng;

sentences.zh: 關中亦號「郡姓」，韋、裴、柳、薛、楊、杜首之；

translations.literal: in Guanzhong they were also called 'commandery surnames'—Wei, Pei, Liu, Xue, Yang, and Du led them;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong likewise had 'commandery surnames,' led by Wei, Pei, Liu, Xue, Yang, and Du;

sentences.zh: 代北則為「虜姓」，元、長孫、宇文、於、陸、源、竇首之。

translations.literal: in the northern frontier they became 'barbarian surnames'—Yuan, Zhangsun, Yuwen, Yu, Lu, Yuan, and Dou led them.
translations.idiomatic: the northern frontier had 'barbarian surnames,' headed by Yuan, Zhangsun, Yuwen, Yu, Lu, Yuan, and Dou.

sentences.zh: 「虜姓」者，魏孝文帝遷洛，有八氏十姓，三十六族九十二姓。

translations.literal: 'Barbarian surnames'—when Emperor Xiaowen of Wei moved the capital to Luoyang, there were eight clans and ten surnames, thirty-six lineages and ninety-two names.
translations.idiomatic: 'Barbarian surnames': when Emperor Xiaowen of Wei moved his capital to Luoyang, there were eight clans and ten surnames, thirty-six tribal lineages and ninety-two family names.

sentences.zh: 八氏十姓，出於帝宗屬，或諸國從魏者；

translations.literal: The eight clans and ten surnames issued from the imperial clan or from the various states that followed Wei;
translations.idiomatic: The eight clans and ten surnames came from the imperial clan or from peoples who had submitted to Wei;

sentences.zh: 三十六族九十二姓，世為部落大人；

translations.literal: the thirty-six lineages and ninety-two names for generations were chieftains of tribal confederations;
translations.idiomatic: the thirty-six tribal lineages and ninety-two surnames had for generations served as tribal chieftains;

sentences.zh: 並號河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: all styled themselves natives of Henan and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: all were registered as natives of Henan and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 「郡姓」者，以中國士人差第閥閱為之制，凡三世有三公者曰「膏粱」，有令、仆者曰「華腴」，尚書、領、護而上者為「甲姓」，九卿若方伯者為「乙姓」，散騎常侍、太中大夫者為「丙姓」，吏部正員郎為「丁姓」。

translations.literal: 'Commandery surnames'—the system ranked Chinese gentry by the graded merits of their clan gates: those with three grand councilors in three generations were called 'fat grain'; those with ministers or vice-ministers were 'rich meat'; those with directors, commissioners, or protectors or above were 'first-grade surnames'; grand masters or regional governors were 'second-grade'; regular attendants or grand masters of splendid happiness were 'third-grade'; full-ranked clerks of the Ministry of Personnel were 'fourth-grade.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Commandery surnames' were classified by the prestige of Chinese gentry clans: three generations of grand councilors earned the title 'fat grain'; ministers or vice-ministers earned 'rich meat'; holders of director or commissioner rank and above were 'first-grade surnames'; nine ministers or regional governors were 'second-grade'; regular attendants or palace counselors were 'third-grade'; full-ranked personnel clerks were 'fourth-grade.'

sentences.zh: 凡得入者，謂之「四姓」。

translations.literal: All who gained entry were called the 'four surnames.'
translations.idiomatic: All who qualified were known collectively as the 'four surnames.'

sentences.zh: 又詔代人諸胄，初無族姓，其穆、陸、奚、於，下吏部勿充猥官，得視「四姓」。

translations.literal: An edict also said that for the various noble lines of the northern dynasties who initially had no clan surnames—such as Mu, Lu, Xi, and Yu—the Ministry of Personnel was ordered not to assign them to base posts, and they were granted equal standing with the 'four surnames.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict further declared that northern noble lines originally without clan surnames—such as the Mu, Lu, Xi, and Yu—were not to be assigned to inferior posts by the Ministry of Personnel but were to be treated on par with the 'four surnames.'

sentences.zh: 北齊因仍，舉秀才、州主簿、郡功曹，非「四姓」不在選。

translations.literal: Northern Qi continued the practice: in recommending cultivated talents, prefectural chief clerks, and commandery merit clerks—those not of the 'four surnames' were not among the candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi maintained the rule: for recommendations of cultivated talent, prefectural chief clerks, and commandery merit clerks—only members of the 'four surnames' were eligible.

sentences.zh: 故江左定氏族，凡郡上姓第一，則為右姓；

translations.literal: Thus in defining clans east of the Yangzi: whatever surname ranked first in a commandery was the prominent surname;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Jiangzuo region defined clans thus: whichever surname ranked first in a commandery counted as a prominent surname;

sentences.zh: 太和以郡四姓為右姓；

translations.literal: under Taihe, the four surnames of a commandery were prominent surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen's Taihe reign, a commandery's four leading surnames counted as prominent surnames;

sentences.zh: 齊浮屠曇剛《類例》凡甲門為右姓；

translations.literal: in the Buddhist monk Tan Gang's Categories and Precedents of Qi, all first-grade gates were prominent surnames;
translations.idiomatic: In the monk Tan Gang's Categories and Precedents of Qi, all first-grade clans were prominent surnames;

sentences.zh: 周建德氏族以四海通望為右姓；

translations.literal: in the clan registry of Jian'ge under Zhou, those of renown throughout the realm were prominent surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Jian'ge clan registry treated families of empire-wide renown as prominent surnames;

sentences.zh: 隋開皇氏族以上品、茂姓則為右姓；

translations.literal: under Sui's Kaihuang clan registry, those of top rank and flourishing surname were prominent surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Sui's Kaihuang registry counted top-rank and flourishing surnames as prominent;

sentences.zh: 唐《貞觀氏族志》凡第一等則為右姓；

translations.literal: in Tang's Zhenguan Register of Clans, all of the first grade were prominent surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Zhenguan Register of Clans treated first-grade families as prominent surnames;

sentences.zh: 路氏著《姓略》，以盛門為右姓；

translations.literal: the Lu clan's Composition on Surnames took flourishing gates as prominent surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Lu's Summary of Surnames took flourishing clans as the standard for prominence;

sentences.zh: 柳沖《姓族系錄》凡四海望族則為右姓。

translations.literal: in Liu Chong's Genealogical Record of Surname Clans, all clans of renown throughout the four seas were prominent surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong's Genealogical Record of Surname Clans counted families of empire-wide standing as prominent surnames.

sentences.zh: 不通歷代之說，不可與言譜也。

translations.literal: One who does not understand the doctrines of successive dynasties cannot speak with him about genealogies.
translations.idiomatic: Without knowledge of how each dynasty defined its clans, one cannot even discuss genealogies intelligently.

sentences.zh: 今流俗獨以崔、盧、李、鄭為四姓，加太原王氏號五姓，蓋不經也。

translations.literal: Now vulgar custom alone takes Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng as the four surnames, adding the Wang clan of Taiyuan and calling them the five surnames—this is largely unfounded.
translations.idiomatic: Popular usage today treats Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng alone as the four great surnames, with the Wang of Taiyuan added to make five—a usage largely without historical basis.

sentences.zh: 夫文之弊，至於尚官；

translations.literal: Now the corruption of refinement came to esteeming office;
translations.idiomatic: When refinement decayed, esteem passed to official rank;

sentences.zh: 官之弊，至於尚姓；

translations.literal: the corruption of office came to esteeming surname;
translations.idiomatic: when office decayed, esteem passed to surname;

sentences.zh: 姓之弊，至於尚詐。

translations.literal: the corruption of surname came to esteeming fraud.
translations.idiomatic: and when surname decayed, esteem passed to fraud.

sentences.zh: 隋承其弊，不知其所以弊，乃反古道，罷鄉舉，離地著，尊執事之吏。

translations.literal: Sui inherited these corruptions, not knowing why they had corrupted; then it reversed the ancient way, abolished village recommendations, severed local registration, and honored the clerks who held affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui inherited this corruption without understanding its cause. Reversing the ancient way, it abolished local recommendations, broke the tie to fixed local registration, and exalted the clerks who actually ran affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是乎土無鄉里，裏無衣冠，人無廉恥，士族亂而庶人僭矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the countryside lacked native districts, villages lacked gentry in caps and robes, people lacked shame, the aristocracy was disordered, and commoners usurped rank.
translations.idiomatic: The countryside lost its native communities; villages lost their gentry; people lost their sense of shame; aristocratic clans fell into disorder, and commoners seized rank beyond their station.

sentences.zh: 故善言譜者，系之地望而不惑，質之姓氏而無疑，綴之婚姻而有別。

translations.literal: Thus one who speaks well of genealogies ties them to regional standing without confusion, verifies them by surname without doubt, and joins them through marriage alliances with clear distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: A master of genealogies, then, anchors records in regional standing without confusion, verifies them against surnames without doubt, and organizes them through marriage alliances with proper distinctions.

sentences.zh: 山東之人質，故尚婚婭，其信可與也；

translations.literal: The people of Shandong are plain, so they esteem marriage alliances—their trustworthiness can be relied upon;
translations.idiomatic: Shandong folk are plainspoken and value marriage alliances—their trustworthiness can be relied on;

sentences.zh: 江左之人文，故尚人物，其智可與也；

translations.literal: the people east of the Yangzi are refined, so they esteem individual character—their intelligence can be relied upon;
translations.idiomatic: the Jiangzuo region is cultured and values personal character—their discernment can be relied on;

sentences.zh: 關中之人雄，故尚冠冕，其達可與也；

translations.literal: the people of Guanzhong are bold, so they esteem caps and official insignia—their attainment can be relied upon;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong folk are forceful and value official rank and insignia—their advancement can be trusted;

sentences.zh: 代北之人武，故尚貴戚，其泰可與也。

translations.literal: the people north of Dai are martial, so they esteem noble kin—their grandeur can be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: the northern frontier is martial and esteems noble kin—their prestige can be relied on.

sentences.zh: 及其弊，則尚婚婭者先外族、後本宗，尚人物者進庶孽、退嫡長，尚冠冕者略伉儷、慕榮華，尚貴戚者徇勢利、亡禮教。

translations.literal: When these declined, those who esteemed marriage alliances put outer clans first and their own lineage second; those who esteemed individuals promoted illegitimate sons and demoted eldest legitimate sons; those who esteemed caps and insignia neglected proper matches and coveted glory; those who esteemed noble kin followed profit and power and abandoned ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: But in their decadence, marriage-alliance advocates favored in-laws over one's own lineage; character advocates advanced bastards over legitimate eldest sons; rank advocates scorned proper marital matches and pursued mere glory; and advocates of noble kin chased power and profit and abandoned ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 四者俱弊，則失其所尚矣。

translations.literal: When all four were corrupt, they lost what they had esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When all four standards rotted, each region lost the very quality it had once prized.

sentences.zh: 人無所守，則士族削；

translations.literal: When people had nothing to hold to, the aristocracy was cut down;
translations.idiomatic: When people had nothing to uphold, the aristocracy withered;

sentences.zh: 士族削，則國從而衰。

translations.literal: when the aristocracy was cut down, the state followed and declined.
translations.idiomatic: when the aristocracy withered, the state declined in turn.

sentences.zh: 管仲曰：「為國之道，利出一孔者王，二孔者強，三孔者弱，四孔者亡。」

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: "The way to govern a state—when benefit issues from one channel one becomes king; from two channels, strong; from three, weak; from four, one perishes."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said: "To govern a state: when all advantage flows through a single channel, one becomes a true king; through two channels, one stays strong; through three, one grows weak; through four, one perishes.

sentences.zh: 故冠婚者，人道大倫。

translations.literal: Therefore cap and marriage are the great bonds of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus capping and marriage are the great bonds of human society.

sentences.zh: 周、漢之官人，齊其政，一其門，使下知禁，此出一孔也，故王；

translations.literal: Zhou and Han in appointing officials aligned their government, unified their gates, and made those below know prohibition—this issued from one channel, therefore they were kings;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han, in selecting officials, unified policy and clan standing so that subjects knew the limits of propriety—advantage flowed through one channel, and so they achieved true kingship;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉官人，尊中正，立九品，鄉有異政，家有競心，此出二孔也，故強；

translations.literal: Wei and Jin in appointing officials honored the Rectifier of the Center, established the nine ranks—districts had divergent policies, households had competing hearts—this issued from two channels, therefore they were strong;
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin honored the Rectifier of the Center and established the nine grades; villages pursued different policies and households competed for advantage—two channels, and so they remained strong;

sentences.zh: 江左、代北諸姓，紛亂不一，其要無歸，此出三孔也，故弱；

translations.literal: the various surnames of Jiangzuo and north of Dai were chaotic and not unified, their essentials had no home—this issued from three channels, therefore they were weak;
translations.idiomatic: the clans of Jiangzuo and the northern frontier were divided and chaotic, with no clear governing principle—three channels, and so they grew weak;

sentences.zh: 隋氏官人，以吏道治天下，人之行，不本鄉黨，政煩於上，人亂於下，此出四孔也，故亡。

translations.literal: The Sui in appointing officials governed the realm by the way of clerks—people's conduct was not rooted in village and district, government was vexed above and people chaotic below—this issued from four channels, therefore it perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui governed through clerical bureaucracy alone; conduct no longer arose from village and district; policy tangled above while the people churned below—four channels, and so the dynasty perished.

sentences.zh: 唐承隋亂，宜救之以忠，忠厚則鄉黨之行修；

translations.literal: Tang inherited Sui's disorder and should remedy it with loyalty—if loyal and sincere, then village and district conduct would be cultivated;
translations.idiomatic: Tang inherited Sui's disorder and should restore it through loyalty; with loyalty and sincerity, village and district conduct would be restored;

sentences.zh: 鄉黨之行修，則人物之道長；

translations.literal: if village and district conduct was cultivated, then the way of individual character would grow;
translations.idiomatic: with village conduct restored, the cultivation of personal character would flourish;

sentences.zh: 人物之道長，則冠冕之緒崇；

translations.literal: if the way of individual character grew, then the thread of caps and insignia would be honored;
translations.idiomatic: with character flourishing, official rank and insignia would regain their prestige;

sentences.zh: 冠冕之緒崇，則教化之風美；

translations.literal: if the thread of caps and insignia was honored, then the wind of transforming instruction would be beautiful;
translations.idiomatic: with rank restored, the tide of moral instruction would run clear;

sentences.zh: 乃可與古參矣。

translations.literal: then one could be compared with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could one stand comparison with the ancients.

sentences.zh: 晉太元中，散騎常侍河東賈弼撰《姓氏簿狀》，十八州百十六郡，合七百一十二篇，甄析士庶無所遺。

translations.literal: In the Taeyuan era of Jin, Regular Attendant Jia Bi of Hedong compiled Register of Surname Records—eighteen provinces, one hundred sixteen commanderies, seven hundred twelve fascicles in all—classifying gentry and commoners without omission.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Taeyuan reign, Regular Attendant Jia Bi of Hedong compiled the Register of Surname Records, covering eighteen provinces and 116 commanderies in 712 fascicles, classifying gentry and commoners without omission.

sentences.zh: 宋王弘、劉湛好其書。

translations.literal: Wang Hong and Liu Zhan of Song liked his book.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong and Liu Zhan of the Liu-Song dynasty prized his work.

sentences.zh: 弘每日對千客，可不犯一人諱。

translations.literal: Hong daily faced a thousand guests yet could avoid violating any single person's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Hong hosted a thousand guests daily yet never once violated anyone's name taboo.

sentences.zh: 湛為選曹，撰《百家譜》以助銓序，文傷寡省，王儉又廣之，王僧孺演益為十八篇，東南諸族自為一篇，不入百家數。

translations.literal: Zhan served in the Selection Bureau, compiled Hundred Clans Genealogy to assist in ranking order—the text was overly terse; Wang Jian expanded it, and Wang Sengru elaborated it into eighteen fascicles; the southeastern clans formed a fascicle of their own, not counted among the hundred clans.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Selection Bureau, Liu Zhan compiled the Hundred Clans Genealogy to assist in ranking candidates. The text was spare; Wang Jian enlarged it, and Wang Sengru expanded it further into eighteen fascicles. The southeastern clans received a separate fascicle, excluded from the main hundred-clan count.

sentences.zh: 弼傳子匪之，匪之傳子希鏡，希鏡撰《姓氏要狀》十五篇，尤所諳究。

translations.literal: Bi transmitted to his son Fei Zhi, Fei Zhi to his son Xi Jing; Xi Jing compiled Essential Records of Surnames in fifteen fascicles, in which he was especially well versed.
translations.idiomatic: Bi passed his work to his son Fei Zhi, who passed it to his son Xi Jing. Xi Jing compiled Essential Records of Surnames in fifteen fascicles, a subject he mastered deeply.

sentences.zh: 希鏡傳子執，執更作《姓氏英賢》一百篇，又著《百家譜》，廣兩王所記。

translations.literal: Xi Jing transmitted to his son Zhi; Zhi further compiled Illustrious Worthies by Surname in one hundred fascicles, and also authored Hundred Clans Genealogy, expanding what the two Wangs had recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jing passed it to his son Zhi, who produced Illustrious Worthies by Surname in one hundred fascicles and also wrote a Hundred Clans Genealogy, expanding the records of the two Wangs.

sentences.zh: 執傳其孫冠，冠撰《梁國親皇太子序親簿》四篇。

translations.literal: Zhi transmitted to his grandson Guan; Guan compiled Genealogical Register of the Liang Imperial Clan's Relatives of the Crown Prince in four fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi passed it to his grandson Guan, who compiled the Genealogical Register of Relatives of the Crown Prince of Liang in four fascicles.

sentences.zh: 王氏之學，本於賈氏。

translations.literal: The Wang clan's learning originated with the Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang lineage's genealogical scholarship traced back to the Jia family.

sentences.zh: 唐興，言譜者以路敬淳為宗，柳沖、韋述次之。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, those who spoke of genealogies took Lu Jingchun as the founder, with Liu Chong and Wei Shu next.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang came to power, genealogical experts regarded Lu Jingchun as their master, with Liu Chong and Wei Shu as the chief successors.

sentences.zh: 李守素亦明姓氏，時謂「肉譜」者。

translations.literal: Li Shousu also understood surnames; the age called him a "living genealogy."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shousu was also expert in surnames and was known in his day as a "living genealogy."

sentences.zh: 後有李公淹、蕭穎士、殷寅、孔至，為世所稱。

translations.literal: Later came Li Gongyan, Xiao Yingshi, Yin Yin, and Kong Zhi, praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Li Gongyan, Xiao Yingshi, Yin Yin, and Kong Zhi, all celebrated in their time.

sentences.zh: 初，漢有鄧氏《官譜》，應劭有《氏族》一篇，王符《潛夫論》亦有《姓氏》一篇，宋何承天有《姓苑》二篇。

translations.literal: Initially, Han had the Deng clan's Official Genealogy; Ying Shao had one fascicle On Clans; Wang Fu's Treatises of a Hidden Gentleman also had one fascicle On Surnames; He Chengtian of Song had two fascicles Garden of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Early works included the Deng clan's Official Genealogy of Han; Ying Shao's one-fascicle On Clans; the Surnames chapter in Wang Fu's Treatises of a Hidden Gentleman; and He Chengtian's two-fascicle Garden of Surnames of Liu-Song.

sentences.zh: 譜學大抵具此。

translations.literal: The learning of genealogies was largely complete in these.
translations.idiomatic: In these works, genealogical scholarship was largely complete.

sentences.zh: 魏太和時，詔諸郡中正，各列本土姓族次第為舉選格，名曰「方司格」，人到於今稱之。

translations.literal: In Wei of the Taihe era, an edict ordered the rectifiers of the center in each commandery to list the order of native surname clans as criteria for recommendation and selection, named "Commandery Rectifier Chart"—people to this day call it by that name.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei's Taihe era, an edict directed each commandery's Rectifier of the Center to rank local clans as standards for recommendation and selection. The result, called the Commandery Rectifier Chart, has been cited ever since.

sentences.zh: 馬懷素，字惟白，潤州丹徒人。

translations.literal: Ma Huaisu, courtesy name Weibai, a native of Dantu in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huaisu, courtesy name Weibai, was a native of Dantu in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 客江都，師事李善，貧無資，晝樵，夜輒然以讀書，遂博通經史。

translations.literal: He sojourned in Jiangdu, studied under Li Shan; being poor and without means, by day he gathered firewood, and at night he always lit a lamp to read books, thus thoroughly mastering the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Jiangdu as a guest, he studied under Li Shan. Penniless, he chopped firewood by day and read by lamplight at night until he had mastered the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，又中文學優贍科，補郿尉。

translations.literal: He passed the presented scholar examination, also passed the Literary Excellence and Generosity examination, and was appointed assistant magistrate of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and the Literary Excellence and Generosity special examination, then was appointed assistant magistrate of Mei.

sentences.zh: 積勞，遷左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service he was transferred to investigating censor of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he was promoted to investigating censor of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 長安中，大夫魏元忠為張易之構謫嶺表，太仆崔貞忄貞、東宮率獨孤祎之祖道，易之怒，使人上急變，告貞忄貞等與元忠謀反。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era, Grand Counselor Wei Yuanzhong was framed by Zhang Yizhi and banished to the Ling region; Vice Master of the Stud Cui Zhenshen and East Palace Commander Dugu Yizhi held a farewell at the road—Yizhi grew angry and sent someone to submit an urgent report of sudden change, accusing Zhenshen and others of plotting rebellion with Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, Grand Counselor Wei Yuanzhong was framed by Zhang Yizhi and exiled to the Lingnan frontier. Vice Master of the Stud Cui Zhenshen and East Palace Commander Dugu Yizhi gave him a roadside farewell. Enraged, Yizhi had an agent file an urgent report accusing Zhenshen and the others of plotting rebellion with Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 武後詔懷素按之，使者促迫，懷素執不從，曰：「貞忄貞餞流人當得罪，以為謀反，則非。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered Huaisu to investigate; messengers pressed him urgently, but Huaisu held firm and would not comply, saying: "Zhenshen sending off an exile should be a crime, but to call it plotting rebellion is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ordered Huaisu to investigate. Messengers pressed him hard, but he refused to comply, saying: "Zhenshen's offense was giving a farewell to an exile; to charge them with treason is wrong.

sentences.zh: 昔彭越以逆誅，欒布奏事屍下，漢不坐罪。

translations.literal: Formerly Peng Yue was executed for treason, yet Luan Bu reported affairs beneath the corpse, and Han did not punish the crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Yue was executed for treason, Luan Bu still made his case before the corpse—and the Han did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 今元忠罪非越比，不宜坐餞闊之人。

translations.literal: Now Yuanzhong's crime is not comparable to Peng Yue's—it is not fitting to implicate those who gave a broad farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong's offense does not compare to Peng Yue's; those who merely paid their respects at his farewell should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 且陛下操生殺柄，欲加之罪，自當處決聖心。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty wields the handle of life and death—if you wish to add guilt, you should yourself decide in your sage heart.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty holds the power of life and death. If you wish to condemn them, that should be your own sovereign decision.

sentences.zh: 既付臣按狀，惟知守陛下法爾。」

translations.literal: Since you have entrusted the case to me to examine, I only know to uphold Your Majesty's law."
translations.idiomatic: But since the case has been entrusted to me, I can only uphold Your Majesty's law.

sentences.zh: 後意解，貞忄貞等乃免。

translations.literal: Later her mind relented, and Zhenshen and the others were spared.
translations.idiomatic: In time the empress relented, and Zhenshen and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 宰相李迥秀藉易之勢，斂賕諉法，懷素劾罷之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Jiongxiu relied on Yizhi's power, collected bribes and evaded the law; Huaisu impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Jiongxiu, trading on Yizhi's influence, took bribes and evaded the law. Huaisu impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以十道使黜陟江西，處決平恕。

translations.literal: As commissioner of the ten circuits for promotion and demotion in Jiangxi, his judgments were even and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as a ten-circuit commissioner to assess officials in Jiangxi, he rendered judgments fairly and with leniency.

sentences.zh: 遷考功，核取實才，權貴謁請不能阿撓。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Bureau of Merit, verified and selected real talent; the powerful who petitioned could not sway him to compromise.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to the Bureau of Merit, he selected genuine talent and could not be swayed by petitions from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 擢中書舍人內供奉，為修文館直學士。

translations.literal: He was elevated to drafting secretary on inner attendance, serving as resident scholar of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafting secretary on inner attendance and appointed resident scholar of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為戶部侍郎，封常山縣公，進兼昭文館學士。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era, he was vice minister of revenue, enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan County, and advanced to concurrent scholar of the Hall of Broad Culture.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan era he became vice minister of revenue, was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan County, and was concurrently appointed a scholar of the Hall of Broad Culture.

sentences.zh: 篤學，手未嘗廢卷。

translations.literal: He was devoted to learning—his hand never put aside a scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted to learning, he never let a book leave his hand.

sentences.zh: 謙恭慎畏，推為長者。

translations.literal: Humble, reverent, cautious, and respectful, he was praised as an elder worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Humble, reverent, and cautious, he was widely regarded as a venerable elder.

sentences.zh: 玄宗詔與褚無量同為侍讀，更日番入。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered him and Chu Wuliang together to serve as lecturing readers, entering on alternating days in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong appointed him and Chu Wuliang as lecturing readers, entering the palace on alternating days.

sentences.zh: 既叩閣，肩輿以進；

translations.literal: Having knocked at the palace gate, he entered by sedan chair;
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at the palace gate, he was carried in by sedan chair;

sentences.zh: 或行在遠，聽乘馬。

translations.literal: if the traveling palace was distant, he was permitted to ride a horse.
translations.idiomatic: and when the emperor was away at a distant residence, he was permitted to ride a horse.

sentences.zh: 宮中每宴見，帝自送迎以師臣禮。

translations.literal: At each palace banquet audience, the Emperor himself saw him off and welcomed him with the ceremony due a teacher-minister.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was received at palace banquets, the emperor himself saw him off and welcomed him with the ceremony due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 有詔句校秘書。

translations.literal: There was an edict to collate the Secretariat at regular intervals.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered periodic collation of the imperial library collections.

sentences.zh: 是時，文籍盈漫，皆炱朽蟫斷，簽紛舛。

translations.literal: At this time documents overflowed everywhere—all were soot-rotted, worm-eaten, and their labels confused and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the archives overflowed with texts, many rotted by soot and worms, their shelf labels jumbled and wrong.

sentences.zh: 懷素建白：「願下紫微、黃門，召宿學巨儒就校繆缺。」

translations.literal: Huaisu submitted a proposal: "I wish Your Majesty to send orders through the Central Secretariat and the Gate of the Yellow, summoning veteran scholars and great Confucians to collate errors and lacunae on the spot."
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu submitted a memorial: "I ask that orders go out through the Central Secretariat and the Gate of the Yellow to summon veteran scholars to collate errors and gaps in the collections.

sentences.zh: 又言：「自齊以前舊籍，王儉《七志》已詳。

translations.literal: He also said: "Old collections before Qi—Wang Jian's Seven Records is already detailed.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "For pre-Qi texts, Wang Jian's Seven Records is already comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 請采近書篇目及前誌遺者，續儉《志》以藏秘府。」

translations.literal: I request collecting recent book titles and sections missing from earlier catalogs, continuing Jian's Records to store in the secret repository."
translations.idiomatic: Please gather recent works and titles omitted from earlier catalogs, extend Jian's Records, and deposit them in the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 即拜懷素秘書監。

translations.literal: Huaisu was immediately appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu was immediately appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乃詔國子博士尹知章、四門助教王直、直國子監趙玄默，陸渾丞吳綽、桑泉尉韋述、扶風丞馬利征、湖州司功參軍劉彥直、臨汝丞宋辭玉、恭陵丞陸紹伯、新鄭尉李子釗、杭州參軍殷踐猷、梓潼尉解崇質、四門直講余欽、進士王愜、劉仲丘、右威衛參軍侯行果、邢州司戶參軍袁暉、海州錄事參軍晁良、右率府胄曹參軍毋煚、滎陽主簿王灣、太常寺太祝鄭良金等分部撰次，踐猷從弟秘書丞承業、武陟尉徐楚璧是正文字。

translations.literal: Then an edict ordered National University Erudite Yin Zhizhang, Four Gates Assistant Instructor Wang Zhi, Direct Attendant of the Directorate of Education Zhao Xuanmo, Assistant Magistrate of Luhun Wu Chuo, Assistant Magistrate of Sangquan Wei Shu, Assistant Magistrate of Fufeng Ma Lizheng, Judicial Administrator of Huzhou Liu Yanzhi, Assistant Magistrate of Linru Song Ciyu, Assistant Magistrate of Gongling Lu Shaobo, Assistant Magistrate of Xinzheng Li Zizhao, Military Administrator of Hangzhou Yin Jianyou, Assistant Magistrate of Zitong Xie Chongzhi, Direct Lecturer of the Four Gates Yu Qin, jinshi Wang Qie and Liu Zhongqiu, Military Administrator of the Right Weiwu Guard Hou Xingguo, Commandery Personnel Clerk of Xingzhou Yuan Hui, Recording Official of Haizhou Chao Liang, Assistant in the Right Victory Guard Fu Ju, Chief Clerk of Yingyang Wang Wan, Grand Sacrificer of the Grand Ancestral Temple Zheng Liangjin, and others to compile sections separately; Yin Jianyou's younger cousin, Secretariat Assistant Yin Chengye, and Assistant Magistrate of Wuzhi Xu Chubi corrected the written text.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed National University Erudite Yin Zhizhang, Four Gates Assistant Instructor Wang Zhi, Direct Attendant of the Directorate of Education Zhao Xuanmo, and a host of local officials and scholars—including Wei Shu, Yin Jianyou, Yu Qin, Wang Qie, Liu Zhongqiu, Hou Xingguo, and Zheng Liangjin—to compile sections in parallel. Yin Jianyou's younger cousin, Secretariat Assistant Yin Chengye, and Wuzhi Assistant Magistrate Xu Chubi corrected the text.

sentences.zh: 懷素奏秘書少監盧俌、崔沔為修圖書副使，秘書郎田可封、康子元為判官。

translations.literal: Huaisu memorialized that Vice Directors of the Secretariat Lu Fu and Cui Mian serve as deputy commissioners for repairing books, and Secretariat Clerks Tian Kefeng and Kang Ziyuan serve as adjudicators.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu recommended Vice Directors Lu Fu and Cui Mian as deputy commissioners for the book restoration project, with Secretariat Clerks Tian Kefeng and Kang Ziyuan as adjudicators.

sentences.zh: 然懷素不善著述，未能有所緒別。

translations.literal: Yet Huaisu was not skilled at writing, and could not organize anything further.
translations.idiomatic: But Huaisu was not a strong writer and was unable to organize the work further.

sentences.zh: 會卒，帝舉哀洛陽南城門，贈潤州刺史，謚曰文，給輿還鄉里，喪事官辦。

translations.literal: Soon he died; the Emperor mourned at the south gate of Luoyang, posthumously granted him Governor of Runzhou, posthumous title Wen, provided a carriage to return to his native district, and had the funeral handled by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died. The emperor mourned at Luoyang's south gate, posthumously appointing him governor of Runzhou with the posthumous title Wen. A state carriage bore his body home, and officials handled the funeral.

sentences.zh: 懷素卒後，詔秘書官並號修書學士，草定四部，人人意自出，無所統一，逾年不成。

translations.literal: After Huaisu died, an edict styled all Secretariat officials as Scholar-Editors of Books; they drafted the four divisions, each following his own mind without unified direction, and after more than a year it was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaisu's death, all Secretariat officials were styled Scholar-Editors of Books. Each drafted entries for the four divisions according to his own judgment, with no unified direction, and after more than a year the project remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 有司疲於供擬，太仆卿王毛仲奏罷內料。

translations.literal: The responsible offices were exhausted by supplying provisions; Vice Master of the Stud Wang Maozhong memorialized to abolish the internal rations.
translations.idiomatic: The supply offices were worn out providing for the project, and Vice Master of the Stud Wang Maozhong memorialized to cut off its internal provisions.

sentences.zh: 又詔右常侍褚無量、大理卿元行沖考絀不應選者，無量等奏：「修撰有條，宜得大儒綜治。」

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Right Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang and Chief Minister of Justice Yuan Xingchong to examine and demote those unfit for selection; Wuliang and the others memorialized: "For compilation there are rules—it is fitting to have a great Confucian oversee the whole."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict directed Right Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang and Chief Minister of Justice Yuan Xingchong to review and demote scholars who failed selection. They memorialized: "Compilation requires rules; a great scholar should oversee the whole effort.

sentences.zh: 詔委行沖。

translations.literal: The edict entrusted it to Xingchong.
translations.idiomatic: The edict put the project in Xingchong's hands.

sentences.zh: 乃令煚、述、欽總緝部分，踐猷、愜治經，述、欽治史，煚、彥直治子，灣、仲丘治集。

translations.literal: Then he ordered Ju, Shu, and Qin to oversee and compile the sections; Jianyou and Qie handled the Classics, Shu and Qin handled Histories, Ju and Yanzhi handled Masters, and Wan and Zhongqiu handled Collections.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong then put Ju, Shu, and Qin in charge of compilation. Jianyou and Qie worked on the Classics; Shu and Qin on Histories; Ju and Yanzhi on Masters; Wan and Zhongqiu on Collections.

sentences.zh: 八年，《四錄》成，上之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Four Catalogues were completed and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Four Catalogues were completed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 學士無賞擢者。

translations.literal: The scholars received no reward or promotion.
translations.idiomatic: None of the scholars received reward or promotion.

sentences.zh: 行沖知麗正院，又奏紹伯、利征、彥直、踐猷、行果、子釗、直、煚、述、灣、玄默、欽、良金與朝邑丞馮朝隱、冠氏尉權寅獻、秘書省校書郎孟曉、揚州兵曹參軍韓覃、王嗣琳，福昌令張悱、進士崔藏之入校麗正書。

translations.literal: Xingchong directed the Lizheng Academy and also memorialized that Shaobo, Lizheng, Yanzhi, Jianyou, Xingguo, Zizhao, Zhi, Ju, Shu, Wan, Xuanmo, Qin, Liangjin, together with Chaoyi Assistant Magistrate Feng Chaoyin, Guanxian Assistant Magistrate Quan Yinxian, Secretariat Proofreader Meng Xiao, Yangzhou Military Administrator Han Qin, Wang Cilin, Fuchang Magistrate Zhang Fei, and jinshi Cui Zangzhi enter to collate Lizheng books.
translations.idiomatic: As director of the Lizheng Academy, Xingchong also recommended Shaobo, Lizheng, Yanzhi, Jianyou, Xingguo, Zizhao, Zhi, Ju, Shu, Wan, Xuanmo, Qin, Liangjin, and others—including Feng Chaoyin, Quan Yinxian, Meng Xiao, Han Qin, Wang Cilin, Zhang Fei, and Cui Zangzhi—to join the collation of Lizheng Academy texts.

sentences.zh: 由是秘書省罷撰緝，而學士皆在麗正矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat ceased compilation, and the scholars were all at Lizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Secretariat stopped compiling books, and the scholars were all assigned to Lizheng.

sentences.zh: 愜、仲丘老病還鄉里。

translations.literal: Qie and Zhongqiu, old and ill, returned to their native districts.
translations.idiomatic: Qie and Zhongqiu, aged and ill, returned home.

sentences.zh: 紹伯卒於官。

translations.literal: Shaobo died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobo died in office.

sentences.zh: 直終岐王府記室參軍事。

translations.literal: Zhi ended as recorder of the Prince of Qi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi ended his career as recorder of the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 玄默集賢直學士。

translations.literal: Xuanmo became a direct scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo became a direct scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 利征，出為山茌令，儒緩無治術，免官，終於家。

translations.literal: Lizheng went out to serve as magistrate of Shanzhi—Confucian and lenient, without governing skill, he was dismissed from office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Lizheng was posted as magistrate of Shanzhi. Gentle and scholarly but lacking administrative skill, he was dismissed and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子釗坐保任非人，終德州長史。

translations.literal: Zizhao was punished for guaranteeing an unworthy man and ended as chief administrator of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhao was punished for vouching for an unworthy man and ended his career as chief administrator of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 欽至太學博士、集賢院學士。

translations.literal: Qin reached Erudite of the Grand Academy and scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Qin rose to Erudite of the Grand Academy and scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 灣，洛陽尉。

translations.literal: Wan served as assistant magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wan served as assistant magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 良金，右補闕、京兆府倉曹參軍事。

translations.literal: Liangjin served as remonstrance official of the right and military storehouse clerk of the capital prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjin served as right remonstrance official and military storehouse clerk of the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寅獻，臨淮太守。

translations.literal: Yinxian served as governor of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Yinxian served as governor of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 曉，左補闕。

translations.literal: Xiao served as left remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao served as left remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 覃，萊州別駕，坐誣告刺史，流遠方。

translations.literal: Qin served as vice governor of Laizhou; he was punished for falsely accusing the governor and was banished to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: Qin served as vice governor of Laizhou but was exiled to a distant region for falsely accusing the governor.

sentences.zh: 藏之，膳部員外郎，明年，以將仕郎梁令瓚文學直書院，後以右率府兵曹參軍而罷，終恒王府司馬。

translations.literal: Zangzhi served as vice director of the Board of Provisions; the next year, as Candidate Gentleman Liang Lingzan served in the Academy of Literary Writings; later he was dismissed as military administrator of the Right Victory Guard and ended as secretary of the Prince of Heng's household.
translations.idiomatic: Zangzhi served as vice director of the Board of Provisions. The next year Candidate Gentleman Liang Lingzan joined the Academy of Literary Writings; later Zangzhi was dismissed as military administrator of the Right Victory Guard and ended as secretary of the Prince of Heng's household.

sentences.zh: 秘書省校書郎源幼良代利征，後以協律郎罷。

translations.literal: Proofreader Yuan Youliang of the Secretariat replaced Lizheng; later he was dismissed as harmonizing official and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat proofreader Yuan Youliang replaced Lizheng; later he was dismissed as harmonizing official and left office.

sentences.zh: 殷踐猷，字伯起，陳給事中不害五世從孫。

translations.literal: Yin Jianyou, courtesy name Boqi, was a fifth-generation collateral descendant of Attendant-in-Ordinary Yin Buhai of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jianyou, courtesy name Boqi, was a fifth-generation collateral descendant of Attendant-in-Ordinary Yin Buhai of Chen.

sentences.zh: 博學，尤通氏族、歷數、醫方。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, he was especially versed in clans, calendrical reckoning, and medical prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned, he was especially expert in clans, calendrical reckoning, and medical prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 與賀知章、陸象先、韋述最善，知章嘗號為「五總龜」，謂龜千年五聚，問無不知也。

translations.literal: He was closest to He Zhizhang, Lu Xiangxian, and Wei Shu; Zhizhang once called him a "fivefold tortoise," meaning that after a thousand years a tortoise gathers knowledge five times and knows all when asked.
translations.idiomatic: He was closest to He Zhizhang, Lu Xiangxian, and Wei Shu. Zhizhang once nicknamed him a "fivefold tortoise"—a tortoise, it was said, gathers wisdom five times in a thousand years and answers every question put to it.

sentences.zh: 初為杭州參軍，舉文儒異等科，授秘書省學士，用曹州司法參軍，兼麗正殿學士。

translations.literal: Initially he served as military administrator of Hangzhou; he passed the Exceptional Literary and Confucian examination, was appointed scholar of the Secretariat, used as judicial administrator of Caozhou, and concurrently served as scholar of the Lizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He began as military administrator of Hangzhou, passed the Exceptional Literary and Confucian examination, was appointed a Secretariat scholar, served as judicial administrator of Caozhou, and concurrently held appointment as a Lizheng Hall scholar.

sentences.zh: 以叔父喪，哀慟歐血而卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: Due to mourning for his paternal uncle, he grieved until he vomited blood and died; he was forty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning his paternal uncle, he grieved so deeply that he vomited blood and died, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 少子寅，舉宏辭，為太子校書，出為永寧尉。

translations.literal: His youngest son Yin passed the Expanded Literary examination, served as proofreader to the Crown Prince, and was appointed magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Yin passed the Expanded Literary examination, served as proofreader to the Crown Prince, and was later posted as magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 吏侮謾甚，寅怒殺之，貶澄城丞。

translations.literal: The clerks insulted and mocked him severely; Yin in anger killed one of them and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When local clerks heaped abuse on him, Yin flew into a rage and killed one of them; he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 病且死，以母蕭老，不忍決。

translations.literal: When he fell ill and was near death, because his mother Xiao was elderly, he could not bear to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When illness brought him close to death, he still could not bring himself to end his life, for his mother Xiao was aged and frail.

sentences.zh: 及斂，其子亮斷指剪發置棺中，自誓事祖母如寅在。

translations.literal: At the encoffining, his son Liang severed a finger and cut his hair, placing them in the coffin, and vowed to serve his grandmother as though Yin were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: At the encoffining, his son Liang cut off a finger and clipped his hair to place in the coffin, vowing to care for his grandmother exactly as Yin would have done.

sentences.zh: 其後侍蕭疾，不脫衣者數年，有白燕巢其楣。

translations.literal: Thereafter he attended Xiao in her illness and for several years did not remove his clothes; white swallows nested on his lintel beam.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he nursed Xiao through her illness and for years never removed his clothes, even to sleep. White swallows built their nest on his lintel beam.

sentences.zh: 後終給事中、杭州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he ended his career as attendant within the Gates and governor of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to attendant within the Gates and governor of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 踐猷弟季友，歷秘書郎，善畫。

translations.literal: Jianyou's younger brother Jiyou served as secretary gentleman and was skilled at painting.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyou's younger brother Jiyou served as a secretariat gentleman and was an accomplished painter.

sentences.zh: 從父仲容，終冬官郎中，有重名。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Zhongrong ended as director of the Winter Office and enjoyed a considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Zhongrong eventually reached the post of director of the Winter Office and enjoyed wide renown.

sentences.zh: 子承業，以謹樸稱，歷太子左諭德、右威衛將軍。

translations.literal: His son Chengye was known for prudence and plainness; he served as left mentor of the Crown Prince and general of the Right Weiji Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengye was celebrated for his sober, unassuming character; he served as left mentor of the Crown Prince and general of the Right Weiji Guard.

sentences.zh: 族子成己，晉州長史。

translations.literal: His clansman Chengji served as chief administrator of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Chengji served as chief administrator of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，母顏叔父吏部郎中敬仲為酷吏所陷，率二妹割耳訴冤，敬仲得減死。

translations.literal: In the beginning, his mother Yan, when her maternal uncle Jingzhong, director in the Ministry of Personnel, was framed by a harsh official, led her two younger sisters in cutting off their ears to appeal for justice; Jingzhong's sentence was reduced from death.
translations.idiomatic: At first his mother Yan, when her maternal uncle Jingzhong, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, was framed by a harsh official, led her two younger sisters in cutting off their ears to plead for justice; Jingzhong's death sentence was commuted.

sentences.zh: 及成己生，而左耳缺雲。

translations.literal: When Chengji was born, his left ear was notched like a cloud.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengji was born, his left ear bore a cloud-shaped notch—as if echoing what his mother had done.

sentences.zh: 孔若思，越州山陰人，陳吏部尚書奐四世孫。

translations.literal: Kong Ruosi was a native of Shanyin in Yuezhou and a fourth-generation descendant of Huan, minister of personnel of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ruosi was a native of Shanyin in Yuezhou and a fourth-generation descendant of Huan, minister of personnel under Chen.

sentences.zh: 祖紹安，與兄紹新蚤知名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao'an, together with his elder brother Shaoxin, was renowned from an early age.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao'an and his elder brother Shaoxin were both celebrated while still young.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，客居鄠，勵誌於學。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he lived as a guest in Hu and devoted himself zealously to study.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Chen, he settled as a guest in Hu and applied himself zealously to his studies.

sentences.zh: 外兄虞世南曰：「本朝淪覆，吾分湮滅，有弟若此，知不亡矣。」

translations.literal: His maternal cousin Yu Shinan said: "Our dynasty has collapsed and fallen; my own share is extinguished—but with a younger brother such as this, I know that all is not lost.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal cousin Yu Shinan said: "Our dynasty has fallen; my own line may be extinguished—but with a younger brother like this, I know the family will not perish.

sentences.zh: 紹安與孫萬壽皆以文辭稱，時謂「孫孔」。

translations.literal: Shao'an and Sun Wanshou were both famed for their literary compositions, and the age called them "Sun and Kong."
translations.idiomatic: Shao'an and Sun Wanshou were both celebrated for their literary gifts, and their contemporaries spoke of them as "Sun and Kong."

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui Daye era, he served as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Sui Daye period he served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 高祖討賊河東，紹安與夏侯端同監軍，禮遇尤密。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor campaigned against rebels in Hedong, Shao'an and Xiahou Duan jointly supervised the army, and the emperor treated them with especial intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor marched against rebels in Hedong, Shao'an and Xiahou Duan jointly served as army supervisors, and the emperor showed them unusual favor.

sentences.zh: 帝受禪，端先歸，拜秘書監。

translations.literal: After the emperor accepted the abdication, Duan returned first and was appointed director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor accepted the throne through abdication, Duan returned to the capital first and was appointed director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 已而紹安間道走長安，帝悅，擢內史舍人，賜宅一區、良馬二匹。

translations.literal: Before long Shao'an made his way by hidden routes to Chang'an; the emperor was pleased and promoted him to gentleman of the Inner Scribe, granting him one residence and two fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shao'an made his way to Chang'an by secret routes; the emperor was delighted and promoted him to gentleman of the Inner Scribe, granting him a residence and two fine horses.

sentences.zh: 若思早孤，其母躬訓教，長以博學聞。

translations.literal: Ruosi was orphaned early; his mother personally taught and instructed him, and as he grew he became known for broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi lost his father early; his mother raised and taught him herself, and he grew to be known for his wide learning.

sentences.zh: 有遺以褚遂良書者，納一卷焉。

translations.literal: When someone bequeathed him writings in Chu Suiliang's hand, he accepted only one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: When someone offered him writings in Chu Suiliang's hand, he accepted only a single scroll.

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「是書貴千金，何取之廉？」

translations.literal: The man said: "This writing is worth a thousand gold—why take so little of it?
translations.idiomatic: The man said: "This calligraphy is worth a thousand in gold—why do you take so little?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「審爾，此為多矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If that is truly so, this is already too much."
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi replied: "If that is truly the case, a single scroll is already more than enough."

sentences.zh: 更還其半。

translations.literal: He then returned half of what had been offered.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned half of what had been offered.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，歷庫部郎中，常曰：「仕宦至郎中足矣。」

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and served as director in the Board of the Treasury; he often said: "In office, reaching the rank of director is enough.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and served as director in the Board of the Treasury. He often remarked: "In public service, reaching the rank of director is enough.

sentences.zh: 座右置止水一石，明自足意。

translations.literal: He placed a stone symbolizing still water by his seat, making clear that he was content with this.
translations.idiomatic: Beside his seat he kept a stone symbolizing still water—a reminder that he was content where he was.

sentences.zh: 中宗初，敬暉、桓彥範當國，以若思多識古今，凡大政事，必咨質後行。

translations.literal: In the early Zhongzong period, when Jing Hui and Huan Yanfan held power, because Ruosi was deeply versed in past and present affairs, on all major state policies they would consult him before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhongzong's reign, while Jing Hui and Huan Yanfan held power, they consulted Ruosi on every major policy beforehand, for he was deeply versed in affairs ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 三遷禮部侍郎，出為衛州刺史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became vice minister of rites and was appointed governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he rose to vice minister of rites, then was appointed governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 故事，以宗室為州別駕，見刺史，驁放不肯致恭。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a member of the imperial clan served as vice governor of a prefecture and met the governor, he would behave insolently and refuse to show proper respect.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing custom, when an imperial clansman served as a prefectural vice governor and came before the governor, he would behave insolently and refuse the proper show of deference.

sentences.zh: 若思劾奏別駕李道欽，請訊狀。

translations.literal: Ruosi submitted an impeachment memorial against Vice Governor Li Daoqin and requested a formal inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi impeached Vice Governor Li Daoqin and requested a formal investigation.

sentences.zh: 有詔別駕見刺史致恭，自若思始。

translations.literal: An edict was issued requiring vice governors to show respect when meeting governors, beginning from Ruosi's case.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued requiring vice governors to show proper deference when meeting governors—a change that began with Ruosi.

sentences.zh: 以清白擢銀青光祿大夫，賜絹百匹，累封梁郡公。

translations.literal: For his integrity he was promoted to silver-blue-gleaming grand master of the glory and granted one hundred bolts of silk; he was cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his integrity he was promoted to silver-blue-gleaming grand master of the glory and awarded one hundred bolts of silk; he was eventually enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 開元七年卒，謚曰惠。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Kaiyuan; his posthumous title was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Kaiyuan and was posthumously titled Hui.

sentences.zh: 從父禎，第進士，歷監察御史，門無賓謁，時譏其介。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Zhen passed the jinshi examination and served as investigating censor; no guests came calling at his gate, and the age mocked him for his austerity.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Zhen passed the jinshi examination and served as investigating censor. Few ever called at his gate, and contemporaries ridiculed him for his stiff reserve.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，再遷絳州刺史，封武昌縣子，謚曰溫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong he was promoted twice to governor of Jiangzhou, enfeoffed as viscount of Wuchang County, and given the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he was twice promoted to governor of Jiangzhou, enfeoffed as viscount of Wuchang County, and posthumously titled Wen.

sentences.zh: 子季詡，字季和。

translations.literal: His son Jixu, courtesy name Jihe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jixu, courtesy name Jihe.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，擢制科，授秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the early Yongchang period he passed the special decree examination and was appointed secretary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongchang era he passed the special decree examination and was appointed a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 陳子昂常稱其神清韻遠，可比衛玠。

translations.literal: Chen Zi'ang often praised him for his lucid spirit and distant elegance, comparing him to Wei Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang often praised his lucid bearing and refined elegance, saying he was the equal of Wei Jie.

sentences.zh: 終左補闕。

translations.literal: He ended as left remonstrance and rectification official.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as left remonstrance and rectification official.

sentences.zh: 若思子至，字惟微。

translations.literal: Ruosi's son Zhi, courtesy name Weiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi's son Zhi, courtesy name Weiwei.

sentences.zh: 歷著作郎，明氏族學，與韋述、蕭穎士、柳沖齊名。

translations.literal: He served as compilation gentleman, was expert in the study of clans, and was famed equally with Wei Shu, Xiao Yingshi, and Liu Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a compilation gentleman, was a leading authority on clans, and stood in equal renown with Wei Shu, Xiao Yingshi, and Liu Chong.

sentences.zh: 撰《百家類例》，以張說等為近世新族，剟去之。

translations.literal: He compiled the "Classification Examples of the Hundred Families"; treating Zhang Yue and others as upstart clans of recent times, he cut them out.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the "Classification Examples of the Hundred Families" and, deeming Zhang Yue and his allies upstart clans of recent times, struck them from the record.

sentences.zh: 說子垍方有寵，怒曰：「天下族姓，何豫若事，而妄紛紛邪？」

translations.literal: Yue's son Ji was then in favor; he said angrily: "Clans throughout the realm—what concern is that of yours, that you should meddle so recklessly?
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Ji was then in high favor and flared with anger: "Clans throughout the realm—what business is that of yours? Why meddle so recklessly?

sentences.zh: 垍弟素善至，以實告。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother had long been on good terms with Zhi and told him what had been said.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother, who had long been close to Zhi, told him exactly what had been said.

sentences.zh: 初，書成，示韋述，述謂可傳。

translations.literal: When the book was first completed, he showed it to Wei Shu, who said it deserved to be handed down.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was first finished, he showed it to Wei Shu, who declared it worthy of publication.

sentences.zh: 及聞垍語，懼，欲更增損，述曰：「止！

translations.literal: When he heard Ji's words, he grew afraid and wished to make further revisions; Shu said: "Stop!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi heard what Ji had said, he grew afraid and wanted to revise the work—but Shu said: "Stop!

sentences.zh: 丈夫奮筆成一家書，奈何因人動搖？

translations.literal: A man who takes up the brush and completes a work of his own—how can he let himself be swayed by others?
translations.idiomatic: When a man takes up the brush and finishes a work that is truly his own, how can he let himself be shaken by other people's words?

sentences.zh: 有死不可改。」

translations.literal: Even facing death, it must not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Even if it costs you your life, the book must not be changed.

sentences.zh: 遂罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 時述及穎士、沖皆撰《類例》，而至書稱工。

translations.literal: At that time Shu, Yingshi, and Chong all compiled works titled "Classification Examples," but Zhi's book was judged the finest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shu, Yingshi, and Chong each wrote a work titled "Classification Examples," but Zhi's alone was judged the finest.
